title: XRP $0.99 Call Draws Scrutiny as Santiment Tracks Growing Shorts
summary: Among the most profitable XRP wallets tracked by Santiment, only one was long as of Nov. 6, while three active short sellers had added about 2.1 million XRP since late October. Santiment paired the data with a trader’s $0.99 call, asking whether a market-wide drop explained its early success. Santim...
content:
Among the most profitable XRP wallets tracked by Santiment, only one was long as of Nov. 6, while three active short sellers had added about 2.1 million XRP since late October. Santiment paired the data with a trader’s $0.99 call, asking whether a market-wide drop explained its early success.

Key Takeaways

  • Three active short sellers added about 2.1 million XRP since late October.
  • Only one of the most profitable XRP wallets tracked by Santiment was long as of Nov. 6, and it hadn’t traded since August.
  • XRP still needed about another 15% drop to hit a trader’s $0.99 target.

Santiment Tracks Bearish Positions Among Profitable XRP Wallets

Short sellers had been adding to bearish XRP positions among the most profitable wallets tracked by blockchain analytics firm Santiment, which shared the data on X on Nov. 6. The firm set its analysis of profitable XRP wallets beside a $0.99 XRP forecast posted by a trader on X, which members of its Score Arena platform were voting on.

Santiment stated:

“A trader called XRP lower, to ~$0.99, and said the call is wrong if XRP closes above $1.36. XRP is down ~10% since.”

Turning to the positions held by profitable XRP accounts it tracked, Santiment added: “Among the most profitable XRP wallets, only one is long, and it hasn’t traded since August. Three active shorts have added ~2.1M XRP since late October.”

In perpetual futures trading, collateral supports positions that provide exposure to gains or losses from price movements without ownership of the underlying tokens. A short position benefits from falling prices, while a long benefits from rising prices. That directional exposure differs from the XRP balances held in spot wallets.

XRP Call Set for Nov. 19 Resolution

Score Arena, Santiment’s platform for funding selected traders, also examined the XRP call and wallet positions on Nov. 6. Santiment questioned how much credit the forecast deserved during widespread selling, asking: “Called it, or lucky timing? The whole market dropped too.” As of that update, another approximately 17% decline was needed to reach the target, the firm estimated. With XRP near $1.16 on Nov. 7, the token would need to fall roughly 15% more to reach $0.99.

Santiment’s Score Arena trader allocation community allows traders to submit forecasts and token holders to back performers. Traders can also support or oppose a posted forecast. Under this allocation model, Santiment assigns its own trading capital to selected participants, while stakers’ tokens stay outside the trades. The company described Score as being in closed beta, a testing phase limited to invited participants, in its Nov. 6 comments.

All three traders who opposed the call on Score had been on the wrong side of XRP’s decline, Santiment reported. Their results remained provisional ahead of the call’s scheduled Nov. 19 resolution. In its Nov. 6 update, the firm also said the prediction window would close in less than two days.

Large XRP Balances Grew Alongside Bearish Trading Positions

Separate Santiment figures showed wallets holding at least 1 million XRP reached 2,147 on Nov. 3, their highest count of 2026. That category had expanded by 28 addresses over 10 days. The balance-based measure tracked addresses crossing a holding threshold, providing a view of large holdings alongside the latest analysis of trading positions.

The XRP Ledger added 7,934 new wallets on Nov. 1, the sixth-highest daily total of the year. Santiment linked a more constructive outlook to daily wallet creation remaining above roughly 4,000 and a recovery above $1.30. A drop below $1.20 alongside daily wallet creation falling under 3,000 would weaken that signal, the firm said.

A Binance XRP scarcity gauge reached a four-year high near 2.1 in a Nov. 5 Cryptoquant analysis. The gauge measures relative XRP availability for trading, with higher readings indicating greater scarcity. Separate figures placed Binance’s total XRP reserves at 2.63 billion that day, up from 2.35 billion on Nov. 3.

title: Amundi Puts a European Equity Fund Share Class on Ethereum
summary: Amundi has launched a tokenised share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on public Ethereum, working with CACEIS. It is a real fund…
content:
TL;DR: Amundi has launched a tokenised share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on public Ethereum, working with CACEIS. It is a real fund share-class initiative, not a claim that all 600 constituent stocks are individually trading as permissionless tokens around the clock.

One of Europe’s biggest asset managers has moved a conventional index product into the world of tokenised fund units. In a November 2026 announcement, Amundi said a new share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 strategy had been issued on public Ethereum, using infrastructure developed with CACEIS.

That matters because asset tokenisation is often discussed in abstract terms. Here, the starting point is an existing diversified European equity strategy and a new way of recording or distributing interests in it.

A tokenised fund is not 600 independently tokenised shares

Amundi’s Core STOXX Europe 600 tracks a broad European equity benchmark. What the firm has announced is a tokenised share class of the fund. It has not said that every underlying company has issued new public blockchain shares or that investors can automatically trade each of those stocks at any hour.

The distinction is fundamental. In a fund structure, an investor owns units governed by the fund’s legal terms. The fund, in turn, holds or tracks the underlying basket according to its mandate. Tokenising the unit can change the infrastructure used for issuance, transfer or recordkeeping without changing the basic economic exposure of the underlying investment strategy.

The company says the traditional distribution model remains available. The Ethereum-linked share class is integrated into the existing operating model rather than replacing the fund’s conventional administration overnight.

Why institutions are interested in the infrastructure

Amundi highlights potential benefits including operational efficiency, quicker settlement, transparency and improved distribution. These are plausible advantages of shared digital records, but each depends on regulatory acceptance, custodianship, identity controls and the systems connecting a blockchain to conventional fund administration.

CACEIS’s role is important because a token cannot, by itself, maintain every legal and administrative function expected of a regulated fund. Shareholder rights, transfer restrictions, reconciliation, accounting and redemption procedures still require well-defined responsible parties.

The effort follows earlier Amundi work involving tokenised money-market products and subscriptions using stablecoins. That progression suggests the asset manager is testing multiple financial use cases rather than assuming one technology will immediately replace existing market infrastructure.

NewsBTC recently examined the NYSE’s planned tokenised securities venue and its transfer-agent partners. The US exchange’s programme and Amundi’s European fund are distinct, but both underline the importance of ownership records and operational plumbing. A blockchain timestamp alone does not resolve an investor-rights question.

What would prove this format has traction?

The most useful measurements will be actual eligible investors using the new share class, the cost and speed of subscriptions and redemptions, secondary-transfer rules and how issuers handle corporate actions and compliance. Amundi has not published enough in the cited announcement to quantify all these outcomes.

There is also no reason to equate demand for tokenised fund units with a guaranteed effect on ETH’s market price. Transaction fees and onchain activity are one component of a much larger network economy, and adoption can grow without a direct one-for-one connection to token valuations.

The development is meaningful because it involves an established asset manager applying public blockchain infrastructure to an actual investment product. The next chapter is operational evidence: whether the new representation makes fund ownership simpler, cheaper or more accessible without compromising the protections investors expect.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Michael Saylor Reveals 400-Year History Behind Bitcoin Income
summary: Michael Saylor traced Strategy’s model of financing bitcoin holdings through income-paying shares to four centuries of financial history. His analysis connected Dutch trading companies, railroad financing, and U.S. tax law to the company’s Stretch security. Saylor Traces Bitcoin Income to Four Centu...
content:
Michael Saylor traced Strategy’s model of financing bitcoin holdings through income-paying shares to four centuries of financial history. His analysis connected Dutch trading companies, railroad financing, and U.S. tax law to the company’s Stretch security.

Key Takeaways

  • Stretch’s initial offering raised approximately $2.521 billion.
  • Daily dividend accrual includes weekends and holidays.
  • Return-of-capital payments reduce investors’ remaining tax basis.

Saylor Traces Bitcoin Income to Four Centuries of Finance

In a Nov. 7 analysis, Michael Saylor, founder and executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (Nasdaq: MSTR), linked the company’s income-producing securities to four centuries of financial history. He described Stretch, Strategy’s variable-rate preferred stock traded as STRC, as a combination of established financing structures and bitcoin reserves. Saylor stated:

“Digital credit took four centuries to make possible.”

The timeline began with the Dutch East India Company, a trading and shipping business chartered in 1602 whose transferable shares allowed investors to exit while capital remained invested. Maryland’s 1836 financing of the Baltimore & Ohio Railroad, a U.S. railway founded in 1827, illustrated early preferred stock. Exchanges and securities regulation later supplied trading infrastructure and legal frameworks.

Preferred shares give investors specified priority over common shareholders for dividends and proceeds distributed when a company is wound down. Creditors rank ahead of both, and these corporate ownership rights differ from owning bitcoin directly. Payments depend on the issuer’s management of its business, assets, and financing.

Stretch Combines Bitcoin Reserves With Preferred Shares

Strategy’s initial Stretch offering closed in July 2025, raising approximately $2.521 billion before expenses, with net proceeds funding 21,021 bitcoins. The preferred shares have no scheduled maturity. A board-determined monthly dividend-rate policy was designed to encourage trading around their $100 stated amount.

Shelf registration lets companies register securities with regulators in advance for sales over time. At-the-market programs then allow issuers to sell new shares into existing markets at prevailing prices. Saylor identified both tools as financing foundations: new issuance brings capital into the business, while trading between existing shareholders transfers ownership.

Repurchases use corporate funds to retire shares and their future dividend claims. In September, Strategy disclosed $176 million in STRC repurchases and expanded its securities repurchase authorization to $2 billion. The authorization reached $3 billion by its October results, followed by $208.2 million of STRC buybacks during Oct. 26-Nov. 1.

Dividend Terms and Tax Rules Shape Investor Payments

An amendment effective Nov. 1 introduced daily STRC dividend accrual, including weekends and holidays. The revised schedule established calendar-day record dates, with payments processed on business days.

Tax rules dating to 1921 supplied another foundation in Saylor’s account. A $12 distribution classified entirely as return of capital would reduce the tax basis of a $100 investment to $88, leaving a $12 gain upon a later $100 sale, before other adjustments. Distributions exceeding the remaining basis generally produce capital gains.

Schwab’s assessment of bitcoin treasury risks explained that cryptocurrency price swings can create earnings volatility and liquidity pressure. STRC carries no collateral claim on Strategy’s bitcoin, leaving payment capacity dependent on the issuer’s resources. The company’s financing, cash reserves, and asset sales provide funds for distributions.

Strategy’s bitcoin sales for dividends and buybacks totaled approximately $431.8 million during 2026 through its October results. Its Nov. 2 filing put the designated dollar reserve at $4.79 billion and separate cash at $132.7 million as of Nov. 1. During Oct. 26-Nov. 1, it paid $43.4 million of preferred dividends from that reserve.

title: Nasdaq Lists Canary’s Staked INJ ETF, Adding Another Route to Altcoin Exposure
summary: Nasdaq began listing the Canary Staked INJ ETF under ticker INJC on November 5, according to the exchange's listing notice and Canary Capital. The product…
content:
TL;DR: Nasdaq began listing the Canary Staked INJ ETF under ticker INJC on November 5, according to the exchange’s listing notice and Canary Capital. The product seeks Injective token exposure and staking rewards, but fund ownership is not the same as directly holding or controlling INJ.

US exchange-traded cryptocurrency products are extending well beyond Bitcoin and Ether. Nasdaq’s November 4 trader notice confirmed that the Canary Staked INJ ETF would be listed starting Thursday, November 5, under the ticker INJC. Canary Capital’s launch announcement describes the fund’s aim as exposure to INJ, the native token of the Injective network, together with an ability to earn staking rewards.

That gives investors a new route into a smaller cryptocurrency using a familiar brokerage account. It also adds a layer of product structure and fees that should not be confused with direct ownership of tokens in a self-custodied wallet.

Price exposure and staking in one wrapper

Injective operates a proof-of-stake blockchain. In proof-of-stake networks, eligible token holders can participate in network validation, often by delegating tokens to validators, and may receive rewards. A staked fund seeks to reflect some of that economics through its holdings and operations.

Canary says net staking rewards will be reflected in the ETF’s net asset value. The word ‘net’ matters: fund expenses, staking arrangements, validator performance and timing can affect the value delivered to shareholders. Investors should examine the prospectus for the risks, fee structure and precise mechanics rather than treating a possible reward as a fixed interest payment.

Nasdaq’s notice identifies the designated liquidity provider and the start of trading and valuation dissemination. That is concrete evidence of a listed product. It does not by itself establish investor demand, daily liquidity under every market condition or what the shares will trade at relative to their underlying net asset value.

A different form of crypto-market access

Spot Bitcoin ETFs have become widely followed because their fund creations and redemptions provide a visible gauge of flows through conventional investment channels. NewsBTC’s recent analysis of Bitcoin ETF outflows illustrates why even those large products can see very different activity from day to day.

A smaller-token fund adds different considerations. The underlying market may be thinner, its network risks more specialised and its investor base less developed than that of Bitcoin. Product suitability depends on the actual structure and an investor’s ability to withstand volatility, not simply on the convenience of buying a ticker.

There is also a difference between a fund seeking staking economics and an account that allows an investor to select their own validator, manage keys or participate directly in onchain governance. The listed wrapper handles custody and operational choices through fund service providers.

What to monitor after launch

The useful follow-up figures are shares outstanding, assets under management, realised flows, bid-ask spreads, trading volumes, fees and how staking income is accounted for. These will tell readers more than a single day’s INJ price move or the excitement surrounding a new listing.

The wider lesson is that the ETF market is developing more specialised structures. That can expand financial access while moving key operational decisions away from end users. INJC’s listing is a verified milestone. Whether it becomes a durable and liquid product remains to be demonstrated by its trading record.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: XRP Is Ripple’s North Star: CEO Centers Strategy on ‘Things That Are Good for XRP’
summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse reaffirmed XRP as the company’s north star, linking RLUSD expansion and business integration to greater liquidity and utility for the crypto asset. His strategy targeted more payments and institutional activity across the XRP ecosystem. Garlinghouse Reaffirms XRP as Ripp...
content:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse reaffirmed XRP as the company’s north star, linking RLUSD expansion and business integration to greater liquidity and utility for the crypto asset. His strategy targeted more payments and institutional activity across the XRP ecosystem.

Key Takeaways

  • Brad Garlinghouse linked RLUSD’s expansion to greater XRP liquidity and utility.
  • Ripple focused on integrating businesses acquired for $2.5 billion in 2025.
  • Treasury and prime brokerage offered paths to move more activity onchain.

Garlinghouse Reaffirms XRP as Ripple’s North Star

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse reiterated his longstanding commitment to XRP in an interview published on Nov. 4. Speaking about the attention surrounding stablecoin Ripple USD (RLUSD), he emphasized: “That wasn’t intended to take away from what we call internally our north star.”

Garlinghouse stated:

“We only want to do things that are good for XRP.”

The executive described RLUSD’s development as serving that objective, explaining that Ripple wanted more payments flowing through Ripple. The asset used for those transactions would depend on the payment corridor and currency pair, while Ripple aimed to keep customers satisfied with that experience.

That position extended his XRP-centered business strategy from February, when he called XRP the north star for Ripple and linked payments, prime brokerage, treasury, custody, and RLUSD to the crypto asset’s development. At XRP Community Day, he identified utility, trust, and liquidity as priorities across those businesses.

RLUSD Expansion Supports the Payments Strategy

In the Nov. 4 video, Garlinghouse said about half of all RLUSD was issued on the XRP Ledger. He stated:

“Our goal is drive as much liquidity, drive as much trust and utility through XRP as possible.”

Ripple described its institutional stablecoin applications as including payments, settlement, and treasury flows. RLUSD is backed one-to-one by cash deposits, U.S. Treasuries, and cash equivalents, according to the company.

For customers settling dollar-denominated obligations, RLUSD offers a dollar-pegged payment asset. Its value is designed to remain stable, while XRP’s price is determined by the market. That distinction allows businesses to transfer a dollar balance while keeping the amount owed and paid expressed in the same currency.

In separate X comments on Nov. 3, Garlinghouse addressed RLUSD’s relationship with XRP by identifying other stablecoins as its competitors. He also expressed a preference for stablecoin use cases running on the XRP Ledger.

Ripple Links Business Integration to XRP Utility

Following $2.5 billion in acquisitions in 2025, Garlinghouse described 2026 as a period of integration. He pointed to growth in the treasury business and opportunities to move traditional payment activity onchain. In prime brokerage, he estimated that roughly 20% of the business was already digital and wanted that share to increase.

His five-year institutional XRP outlook similarly connected the token with Ripple’s expansion beyond payments. In a separate Swell video shared Oct. 28, Garlinghouse envisioned XRP developing as institutional financial infrastructure. He favored using it where it suited customer transactions, preferring a small share of their activity over none.

Beyond Ripple, XRP treasury holdings and team payments reflected a similar commitment at Anodos Finance, a developer of XRP Ledger trading and wallet tools. Its co-founder and CEO, Panos Mekras, stated on May 31 that the company had bought XRP for its treasury, held the asset, and paid its team with it since 2023. He described XRP use on the XRP Ledger, Solana, which supports decentralized applications, and Flare, which connects applications with external data.

title: Chainalysis Begins Restoring Screening Services After Disclosing Exposed Password Hashes
summary: Chainalysis said on November 6 it was restoring KYT and address screening in phases after a cyberattack. The firm earlier disclosed that names, usernames,…
content:
TL;DR: Chainalysis said on November 6 it was restoring KYT and address screening in phases after a cyberattack. The firm earlier disclosed that names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for users had been exposed. Customers were told to prepare password resets and API-key rotation; investigations data exposure has not been established.

A disruption at one of cryptocurrency’s best-known investigative and compliance providers is also a test of operational resilience for the companies that depend on it. In a security incident notice updated November 6, Chainalysis said it had begun restoring access to its Know Your Transaction, or KYT, and address-screening products through a phased process.

The restoration followed several days of service restrictions and increasingly detailed disclosures about a cyberattack. Because many crypto businesses use screening tools to investigate suspicious transactions or meet compliance obligations, this is a story about both information security and the ability of regulated operations to continue.

The company’s disclosures evolved during the week

Chainalysis initially reported discovering unauthorised activity affecting its internal systems and tools. Its October 30 statement said it had found no evidence at that point of access to certain sensitive materials. But the November 4 update disclosed that user information, including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens, had been exposed to an attacker.

That sequence is important. Early incident statements often reflect a limited investigation, and later forensic work can establish a wider impact. The responsible reading is the latest dated disclosure, not a permanently frozen version of the first announcement.

The company also reported abnormal activity around KYT and other screening tools, prompting additional products to be taken offline. Chainalysis said it had no evidence of access to investigation content or manipulation of its attribution data at the time of its updates. That is a narrower claim than declaring every possible effect ruled out.

Passwords and API credentials require attention

Chainalysis told customers to submit trusted IP addresses for allowlisting and prepare to reset passwords and rotate API keys as access is restored. A password hash is not the same as a plaintext password, but exposed hashes create security concerns depending on how they were generated and the strength of the underlying credentials. Live tokens can present a separate risk because they may enable access while valid.

For organisations, the operational response should follow the vendor’s direct instructions and their own security teams’ assessment. Users should not click unexpected reset links in unsolicited emails; signing in through a verified service address is safer than relying on a message that could be spoofed.

The wider issue of controls and dependency is also present in NewsBTC’s coverage of Aave’s protective restrictions on new tBTC positions. Different systems and risks are involved, but both illustrate how a provider’s status can affect the options available to dependent services.

Screening outages are a market infrastructure problem

Compliance teams need accurate screening, audit trails and clear decisions about when they can accept funds or process an onboarding request. Temporarily losing a primary tool can complicate those processes even if the underlying blockchain continues operating. Backups, manual escalation and incident playbooks are therefore part of real crypto infrastructure.

Chainalysis said restoration would expand as it validated enhanced security controls. It had not, in the cited November 6 update, confirmed full restoration of every affected product. That distinction should guide reporting and customer decisions.

The key future questions are the complete scope of exposure, remedial actions, the timetable for Reactor and other affected products and independent assurance that compromised credentials have been invalidated. For now, the firm has acknowledged a serious security incident and begun a controlled recovery.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: EU Deploys Dedicated Crypto Task Force to Block Russian Evasion
summary: The new crypto task force will be part of a new sanctions office that will coordinate how national authorities apply the rules to avoid circumvention of these measures using digital assets, targeting crypto networks like A7, which provided a digital ruble stablecoin to skirt these restrictions. EU L...
content:
The new crypto task force will be part of a new sanctions office that will coordinate how national authorities apply the rules to avoid circumvention of these measures using digital assets, targeting crypto networks like A7, which provided a digital ruble stablecoin to skirt these restrictions.

Key Takeaways

  • The EU formed a new crypto task force to close loopholes letting Russia evade sanctions with digital assets.
  • The 12-month initiative unites member states to disrupt networks like the A7 stablecoin and maximize impact.
  • This aligns with broader EU jurisdiction bans and US crackdowns on exchanges moving illicit Russian funds.

EU Launches Crypto Task Force to Curb Russian Digital Asset Networks

As countries like Russia increasingly use digital assets to circumvent traditional sanctions, enforcement organizations are also targeting these networks.

At the EU’s tenth high-level meeting on union restrictive measures, the Commission convened to create a dedicated sanctions office to analyse how the EU applies sanctions against Russia and how the country is adapting to circumvent them.

Maria Luís Albuquerque, Commissioner for Financial Services and the Savings and Investments Union, reported that the meeting focused on “turning sanctions into concrete results: closing loopholes, tackling circumvention and ensuring consistent implementation across the EU.”

The sanctions office will strengthen coordination between member states to deliver a more effective application of these restrictive measures, bringing together several aspects of the sanctions lifecycle, including policy design, implementation, enforcement support and anti-circumvention.

Specifically, the office seeks to close loopholes that allow Russia to keep operating, maximizing the impact of these restrictions on the Russian economy.

Sitting inside the office, a new crypto task force was created to deal with the utilization of digital assets to skirt sanctions, an area where the EU has been especially active since July, when the bloc targeted the complete Russian crypto ecosystem in its 20th sanctions package.

“We know that crypto is a tool that has been used to circumvent our sanctions,” said EU spokesperson Siobhan McGarry. A7A5, a digital ruble stablecoin, registered transaction volumes of over $100 billion before facing a sanctions attack that dismantled a US dollar-based exchange network, effectively thwarting its usability and cratering operational volumes.

According to the Kyiv Independent, the task force is expected to work for 12 months and will have support from countries like Ukraine and the UK, which have already targeted Russian crypto networks before.

Acknowledging the rapid development of the ecosystem, in its 21st package of sanctions against Russia, the EU introduced the possibility of banning entire crypto jurisdictions, ordering European exchanges to stop transactions with cryptocurrency services established in specific named nations.

The U.S. is also tightening its crypto oversight. Recently, Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) blacklisted MEXC, a cryptocurrency exchange, for processing at least $16 billion in suspicious transactions between May 2021 and May 2026 linked to sanctioned entities in Iran, North Korea, and Russia.

title: Zcash Activates NU7 With 25-Second Block Target and New Fee Reserve
summary: Zcash's NU7 upgrade activated at mainnet block 3,543,405, reducing target block spacing from 75 to 25 seconds. It also changes how fees contribute to future…
content:
TL;DR: Zcash’s NU7 upgrade activated at mainnet block 3,543,405, reducing target block spacing from 75 to 25 seconds. It also changes how fees contribute to future network security. Faster target blocks do not make every payment final instantly, and node operators need compatible software.

Zcash has crossed an important protocol milestone. The NU7 network upgrade activated in early November at block height 3,543,405, bringing a faster target block interval and changes to the economics of future block rewards. The Zcash Foundation’s Zebra 7 release notes identify the same mainnet activation height and describe the consensus changes required for nodes to follow the chain.

The upgrade is not just a software patch. It changes how Zcash produces blocks and how some transaction fees are handled, while preserving the wider coin-issuance framework.

What moving from 75 to 25 seconds changes

Zcash’s new target is a block every 25 seconds, down from 75 seconds before the upgrade. In theory, that means users and services waiting for several confirmations can receive them sooner. But target spacing is a statistical expectation, not a service-level guarantee: real blocks arrive irregularly, and exchanges or payment processors choose their own confirmation policies.

To prevent a tripling of the number of blocks from mechanically tripling new coin issuance, the upgrade scales the scheduled reward per block and adjusts remaining issuance and halving intervals. The idea is to deliver more frequent blocks while keeping the rate of monetary issuance broadly aligned with the previous schedule.

The node-software detail matters as much as the headline speed. Zebra’s release notes say operators must upgrade to a NU7-compatible client to remain on the consensus chain after the activation point. A user may experience difficulties if a wallet or service depends on an outdated node even when the network itself is operating normally.

A mechanism for later security funding

NU7 also introduces a Network Sustainability Mechanism that directs a portion of transaction fees into a public reserve for future reissuance to miners. Accounts of the upgrade put that reserve contribution at 60% of fees, with the remaining 40% available to miners at the time of collection. The stated design goal is to smooth the eventual decline in subsidy-funded security spending as the network matures.

That is a policy choice within a public cryptocurrency, not free revenue. Money reserved for future rewards is not available in the same way as fees paid immediately to today’s miners. Evaluating the mechanism means examining incentives over time, its interaction with market demand and whether it achieves the intended security effects.

The change also retires support for older version-four transactions, affecting Zcash’s original Sprout pool. This is a reminder that long-running blockchains can carry technical baggage that becomes increasingly difficult to maintain, especially when privacy features and proof systems evolve.

Faster confirmations still need an operational reality check

Zcash offers privacy-preserving transfers, so network improvements should also be assessed against wallet compatibility, scanning performance and the accessibility of shielded payments. The upgrade can improve the underlying capability without ensuring every exchange, mobile wallet or merchant adopts the same features immediately.

NewsBTC previously examined the network’s Zebra synchronisation work ahead of NU7, when the emphasis was on nodes following the chain reliably. Activation does not eliminate those operational responsibilities.

For users and operators, the practical next checks are node versions, observed block times, confirmation requirements and whether particular wallets have published NU7 support notices. The verified milestone is a mainnet rule change; its day-to-day value will emerge through reliability and actual private-payment usage.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Featured image: Zcash project emblem (illustrative brand mark for Zcash NU7 network upgrade coverage). Source: Zcash project via Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain simple logo).

title: Nigeria Sets New Stablecoin Licensing Rules and Capital Requirements
summary: Nigeria's central bank issued a new framework on November 5 for non-security virtual assets, with separate stablecoin licences tied to naira and…
content:
TL;DR: Nigeria’s central bank issued a new framework on November 5 for non-security virtual assets, with separate stablecoin licences tied to naira and foreign-currency tokens. The rules introduce reserve, capital and local-presence obligations and ban certain algorithmic designs. This is a payments-regulation story, not a blanket legalisation of every crypto activity.

Nigeria is moving from broad policy debates over digital assets toward detailed rules for the businesses that issue and move them. In a November 5 circular and accompanying regulations, the Central Bank of Nigeria set out a licensing framework covering stablecoins, payment services, custody, transfers and remittances involving non-security virtual assets.

The framework is relevant well beyond Nigeria because international stablecoin businesses cannot assume that having a foreign issuer or a smart contract operating outside the country puts them outside its reach.

Two stablecoin classes, with different obligations

The central bank differentiates between naira-referenced stablecoins and those referencing foreign currencies. Class 1 covers naira-linked issuers; Class 2 addresses foreign-currency-backed tokens. Reporting on the regulation has highlighted minimum paid-up capital requirements of 10 billion naira for Class 1 and 15 billion naira for Class 2, with the bank retaining power to prescribe higher amounts.

Each token also requires approval. The regulator’s rules set out information that must be provided about reserves, redemption processes, supported networks, governance and risks. This is a significantly more demanding proposition than deploying a dollar-token smart contract and putting a logo on a website.

The rules are designed around backing and redemption, including restrictions on algorithmic arrangements that rely primarily on market mechanisms rather than eligible reserve assets to maintain value. Customers therefore need to consider not only whether a token trades near its peg but whether its issuer can honour redemptions and safeguard assets during stress.

Cross-border operators cannot ignore local rules

According to the circular, the framework applies to regulated activities conducted in or from Nigeria, directed at Nigerian residents, or materially affecting Nigerian payment and financial systems. Physical absence is not necessarily an exemption. That means an international stablecoin platform may have licensing and local-incorporation questions to answer before actively targeting the market.

The central bank also distinguishes its payments and non-security remit from the Nigerian securities regulator’s responsibilities. An investment-like token can trigger separate oversight. The exact legal classification of a digital product matters more than the marketing term ‘crypto’.

The regulatory separation recalls NewsBTC’s examination of Coinbase’s EEA restrictions on particular stablecoins. Both examples show that a token can continue existing on a blockchain while platforms’ ability to offer it to users changes by jurisdiction.

A compliance test for issuers and payments firms

The Nigerian framework covers anti-money-laundering checks, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, safeguarding and customer disclosures. These duties can be expensive, particularly for smaller firms, but the regulator is explicitly prioritising consumer protection and financial-system integrity alongside innovation.

There are transitional provisions for existing operators; firms should read the official text to establish their own deadline and authorisation obligations rather than assume a news headline provides legal advice. Any commercial forecast about how many licences will be issued is premature.

For users, the real test will be whether licensed products provide dependable redemption, transparent fees and practical access to cross-border payments. For issuers, it will be whether they can meet the reserve and governance requirements while retaining useful economics. Nigeria has supplied a much clearer regulatory framework, but the market’s response still has to be measured through actual compliant launches.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Gnosis Pay Data Breach Exposes Sensitive Customer Records
summary: Gnosis Pay confirmed a data breach on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, after unauthorized access to its legacy consumer card system exposed customer information. One affected user reported that his name, home address, card number, and linked cryptocurrency wallets were compromised, although the company says cu...
content:
Gnosis Pay confirmed a data breach on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, after unauthorized access to its legacy consumer card system exposed customer information. One affected user reported that his name, home address, card number, and linked cryptocurrency wallets were compromised, although the company says customer funds remain secure.

Key Takeaways

  • Gnosis Pay detected unauthorized access on Nov. 3, 2026, and disclosed the data breach Nov. 6, initiating containment within two hours of detection.
  • Rotki founder Lefteris Karapetsas reported that exposed information included his full name, home address, card number and linked cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
  • The affected consumer card system is scheduled for retirement Dec. 20, 2026, while the company’s enterprise platform was reportedly unaffected.

What Happened to Gnosis Pay?

The cryptocurrency payment provider disclosed the incident three days after monitoring systems identified unauthorized access. According to Gnosis Pay’s data breach update, the intrusion affected its business-to-consumer (B2C) card infrastructure, rather than the enterprise platform supporting its white-label payment programs.

“On 3 November 2026, our monitoring systems detected unauthorised access to the system powering Gnosis Pay-branded cards (our B2C business line), resulting in the exposure of certain customer information,” the company explained.

Gnosis Pay stressed that its security personnel responded immediately, initiating containment within two hours of detection. The company subsequently replaced affected credentials and addressed the vulnerability responsible for the intrusion.

“The data breach was limited to the system powering Gnosis Pay-branded cards, which was already scheduled for retirement on 20 December 2026,” Gnosis Pay stated. “Our enterprise platform, which powers all of our white-label card programmes, was not affected.”

The company has not publicly disclosed how many customers were compromised, nor has it published a comprehensive inventory of exposed information. Instead, affected cardholders received individualized notifications detailing which account records were accessed.

Gnosis Pay Wallet Addresses Exposed Alongside Names and Home Addresses

The potential consequences extend beyond conventional payment-card fraud. Lefteris Karapetsas, founder of cryptocurrency portfolio tracker Rotki, reported that his compromised information included his full name, residential address, card number and every cryptocurrency wallet address associated with his account.

“Extremely disappointed. You had already lost me as a user but you could have at least protected my data…. Damn shame, really,” Karapetsas wrote.

The disclosure illustrates an uncomfortable contradiction surrounding self-custodial cryptocurrency payments. Although customers retain control of their digital assets, centralized payment infrastructure can still accumulate information connecting identifiable individuals to publicly traceable blockchain addresses.

Such combinations create opportunities for targeted phishing, impersonation and potentially physical intimidation, particularly when residential addresses accompany financial information. However, the available disclosures do not establish that the exposed records have already been exploited for those purposes.

Karapetsas wasn’t the only one disappointed. “Can you shut down tomorrow so there is no third hack please?” one X user replied to the Gnosis Pay X post on the subject. “What address should I use to sue the shit out of you?” another X account asked.

Gnosis Pay Adds 3D Secure Checks After Security Breach

Gnosis Pay has introduced mandatory 3D Secure verification for online card payments while increasing monitoring of suspicious card and wallet activity. These protections will remain active until the consumer system’s scheduled Dec. 20 retirement.

“We sincerely apologise,” the company declared. Gnosis Pay added:

“We understand how serious it is to have your personal information exposed, and we deeply regret that this happened. While funds were not affected, we recognise that the security of personal information is just as important.”

The provider also notified its partners and card issuer while communicating with relevant data protection authorities. Gnosis Pay said it is conducting a comprehensive security review and arranging specialist monitoring for evidence of stolen information being misused. The company cautioned:

“Be suspicious of any unexpected email, text, call or letter about Gnosis Pay, a Partner App or your card, even if it includes your real details or a real purchase.”

“Never share your seed phrase, private keys, PIN or full card number,” Gnosis Pay added, emphasizing that legitimate representatives will never request sensitive credentials or instruct customers to transfer funds through unsolicited communications.

The November disclosure follows a separate June 2026 incident involving Gnosis-related infrastructure that reportedly resulted in approximately $1.5 million to $1.8 million in losses, which Gnosis subsequently covered.

Unlike that incident, the latest breach principally threatens personal privacy rather than immediate asset custody. Nevertheless, the distinction offers limited comfort when compromised identity records can permanently associate individuals with transparent blockchain transactions.

Retiring vulnerable infrastructure may eliminate future exposure through that system, but it cannot reverse the disclosure of sensitive personal information. Gnosis Pay says customer funds remain safe, yet exposed identities, residential addresses, and cryptocurrency wallet connections present privacy risks that cannot simply be undone.

The Gnosis Pay incident follows a long string of crypto industry data breaches in 2026. Ledger exposed customer information in January, followed by Safepal’s leak affecting nearly 40,000 customers and Trezor’s breach involving roughly 81,000 people. Keystone suffered an October intrusion exposing nearly 26,000 buyer records, while Chainalysis disclosed a breach involving user credentials and authentication tokens.

title: US Adds 165,000 Jobs in October: Why Bitcoin Traders Are Watching the Fed
summary: The US economy added 165,000 payroll jobs in October while unemployment stood at 4.1%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' November 6 release. The…
content:
TL;DR: The US economy added 165,000 payroll jobs in October while unemployment stood at 4.1%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ November 6 release. The data complicate hopes of quick monetary easing, but the report by itself cannot establish what the Federal Reserve will do next or where Bitcoin will trade.

Bitcoin’s difficult trading week has coincided with a closely watched update on the US economy. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on November 6 that nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 in October. The unemployment rate was little changed at 4.1%.

For cryptocurrency traders, the significance is not that payrolls have a mechanical relationship with Bitcoin’s price. Rather, employment data are one part of the evidence the Federal Reserve weighs when deciding whether inflation and economic activity justify changing interest rates.

The headline numbers tell only part of the story

The BLS said employment increased in professional and business services, healthcare, and transportation and warehousing. Professional and business services added 70,000 jobs, substantially above that category’s recent monthly average. The report also revised August and September gains upward by a combined 84,000 jobs.

Those revisions matter because monthly payroll estimates are not fixed snapshots of economic reality. More complete information can materially alter the picture after the first publication. Anyone building a large market argument on a single month should therefore examine the trend and the revisions, not only the latest number.

Average hourly earnings for private-sector employees rose by 0.4% in October and 3.1% over 12 months, according to the same release. Wage developments can affect the inflation outlook, although inflation depends on many other factors including productivity, goods costs and service-sector conditions.

Why rates matter for risk assets

When investors expect a lower path for policy rates, the relative attraction of cash and short-duration interest-bearing assets may fall, potentially supporting risk assets. A stronger labour market can complicate that narrative by giving policymakers less reason to ease quickly. But the Fed’s response depends on the whole data set, not an automatic rule that more jobs always mean higher rates.

Bitcoin is not a conventional corporate security with earnings that can be discounted using a single valuation model. Even so, it trades within financial markets where leverage costs, dollar liquidity and investor risk appetite change with the broader macroeconomic environment. That connection can become particularly visible during sharp stock-market moves.

There is also a separate institutional channel. NewsBTC reported that spot Bitcoin ETFs suffered $398.6 million in net withdrawals on November 2, reflecting flows into and out of listed investment products. Those fund numbers are useful but do not show why each investor traded.

What happens next is an open question

Market commentary has linked recent cryptocurrency weakness to technology-stock volatility and changing interest-rate expectations. That can be a plausible interpretation of contemporaneous movements, but correlation is not proof of one exclusive cause. Leverage, derivatives positioning and crypto-specific events may be operating at the same time.

The important next readings include inflation releases, future employment revisions and Federal Reserve communications. Traders should also follow the distinction between network fundamentals and investment-market behaviour explored in NewsBTC’s hashrate coverage. A shift in financial conditions can affect market prices long before it changes the underlying protocol.

For now, October’s jobs report provides a firmer data point in the interest-rate debate. It does not supply a confident Bitcoin price target or a guaranteed forecast for the next Fed decision.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Solo Bitcoin Miners Strike Digital Gold as 2026 Jackpot Wins Reach 36 Blocks
summary: A tiny bitcoin mining machine beat astronomical odds during the first week of November, adding another unlikely victory to a year of solo mining jackpots. From compact desktop devices to industrial-scale competitors, 2026 has delivered 36 documented solo-style block discoveries worth millions of dol...
content:
A tiny bitcoin mining machine beat astronomical odds during the first week of November, adding another unlikely victory to a year of solo mining jackpots. From compact desktop devices to industrial-scale competitors, 2026 has delivered 36 documented solo-style block discoveries worth millions of dollars.

Key Takeaways

  • Soloblocks.io recorded 36 solo-style Bitcoin blocks from Feb. 11 through Nov. 7, 2026, with rewards ranging from 3.1268 BTC to 3.1968 BTC.
  • Solo Satoshi reported that a NerdQAxe++ Rev 6 successfully found block 974238, although that block is not included in Soloblocks.io’s dataset because it wasn’t a true solo block and the miner was leveraging Braiins non-solo pool.
  • Entry-level mining machines can produce approximately 1.2 TH/s, compared with a Bitcoin network operating at 1,000 exahash per second (EH/s).
  • At least 17 solo mining pools, services and configurations offer different approaches to chasing block rewards, including traditional solo mining and different types of shared-payout arrangements.

A Tiny Bitcoin Miner Takes on the Giants and Wins

Imagine buying a modest desktop mining machine, plugging it into a wall socket, and discovering that your little contraption has beaten an army of industrial competitors to a block reward worth 3.125 BTC plus fees. It sounds like winning the lottery with a ticket that never stops playing.

That is precisely the attraction of solo bitcoin mining, where ordinary enthusiasts compete against warehouses filled with specialized mining equipment. Most participants will never find a block, but every valid hash represents another microscopic opportunity to claim the prize.

On Nov. 5, 2026, Solo Satoshi, a retailer specializing in small-scale bitcoin mining hardware, highlighted another extraordinary discovery involving one of its customers.

The company announced on X:

“Block#974238 has been claimed. ANOTHER ONE of our devices has hit a block by a NerdQAxe++ Rev 6. This afternoon, a very early Solo Satoshi customer DM’d Kels so she could let the team know. Just a month ago, another person came to the store to tell us he found a block while running a Bitaxe Naja Duo and a NerdQAxe++ Rev 7. Both running Braiins fpps pool. Keep hashing. You never know when your hardware might be next!”

The announcement offers a compelling example of small mining hardware participating in successful block discovery. However, Braiins FPPS is a shared-reward pool, meaning the machines’ participation does not establish that their owners individually collected entire block rewards.

Three days later, the operator of CKPool Solo disclosed on X that an independent miner commanding just over half a petahash of computing power had successfully mined block height 974893. “Congratulations to miner bc1q~nljg for solving the 319th now lucky block at US East [CKPool Solo] with ~581TH of hashrate on a 564TH worker.”

The developer behind CKPool Solo added:

“A miner of this size has about a one in 35 chance of solving a block in a year.”

Following that block, hours later on Nov. 7, another solo block was discovered from a CKPool Solo mining participant. “Two lucky solo miners found blocks today on CKPool, just seven hours apart,” the mempool.space developer Mononaut wrote on Saturday.

Bitcoin’s 2026 Solo Mining Jackpot Reaches 36 Documented Blocks

According to Soloblocks.io data, bitcoin miners associated with solo-style operations discovered 36 blocks between Feb. 11 and Nov. 7. The recorded rewards totaled approximately 113.149 BTC, including transaction fees, representing a solid handful of mining prizes worth around $8.5 million today.

Using the current bitcoin price, individual rewards were worth approximately $236,500 to $241,700. Those figures represent gross block rewards rather than confirmed take-home proceeds, and pool arrangements can change how much any participant receives.

The earliest recorded discovery occurred Feb. 11 at block 936100 through the multi-coin mining pool Letsmine.it, paying 3.1529 BTC. February produced four recorded discoveries, followed by six in April, three in May, two in June, four in July, one in August, and one in September.

October delivered eight discoveries, while November accounted for seven through Nov. 7. The November concentration included four blocks on Sunday, Nov. 1, another on Thursday, Nov. 5, and the two CKPool Solo blocks that were discovered on Friday, Nov. 6, and Saturday, Nov. 7.

The distribution also reveals an important qualification. Not every so-called solo winner was an ordinary hobbyist with a single inexpensive machine. The Soloblocks.io archive identifies some operations as small farms, including estimated hashrates of 153.7 petahash per second (PH/s) and 540 PH/s, substantially exceeding consumer mining equipment, yet small potatoes compared to today’s mega mining pools.

Public Pool’s five recorded discoveries, by contrast, were classified as home-miner jackpot finds. Three involved Umbrel nodes, demonstrating how independent mining infrastructure can participate without requiring an industrial operation.

Across the 36 discoveries, Soloblocks.io’s dataset attributes ten to a category labeled Solo Pool, nine to CKPool Solo, five each to Public Pool, Braiins Solo, and Parasite Pool, and one each to Futurebit Apollo Solo and Letsmine.it.

The Machines Behind Bitcoin’s Lottery Mining Craze

Bitcoin lottery miners span an extraordinary range of power requirements and computing capabilities. For instance, a Bitaxe Gamma 601 or 602 produces approximately 1.2 terahash per second (TH/s) while consuming 17 to 20 watts.

The NerdQAxe++ Rev 7, associated with Solo Satoshi’s previously mentioned X post, produces approximately 4.8 TH/s using four BM1370 chips. The Bitaxe Naja Duo 1201 offers approximately 4.4 TH/s at 42 watts, while the larger NerdOctaxe Gamma reaches roughly 8 TH/s.

Other contenders include Canaan’s Avalon Nano 3S, rated at 6 TH/s and 140 watts, and Futurebit’s Apollo II, with a claimed 6 to 10 TH/s operating range. The Apollo line also offers integrated Bitcoin node functionality, allowing users to operate more independently.

At the novelty end sits the Nerdminer, an ESP32-based device producing only kilohashes per second. It demonstrates the mining process but has effectively negligible chances of discovering a block.

The difference between these machines matters, but not nearly as much as newcomers might expect. Even a relatively powerful 10 TH/s desktop miner contributes only one hundred-millionth of the 1,000 EH/s powering the Bitcoin network today.

Under that simplified network assumption, a 10 TH/s machine would expect to discover one block approximately every 1,900 years. A 1.2 TH/s Bitaxe faces an expected wait exceeding 15,000 years. These machines are mere minnows in an ocean of industrial giants, dwarfed by today’s next-generation ASIC miners, some of which pack a staggering 1 PH/s of hashing power.

Those figures describe statistical averages, not waiting periods that miners must complete. Every attempt is independent, meaning a machine could theoretically find a block tomorrow or run for generations without success.

That mathematical absurdity is exactly what makes a successful home-miner discovery so fascinating.

Solo Pools Offer Different Ways to Chase the Prize

For enthusiasts unwilling to operate their own complete mining infrastructure, solo mining pools provide accessible entry points. Unlike conventional pooled mining, genuine solo arrangements generally award the successful finder the block reward, minus applicable fees.

The prominent CKPool Solo charges approximately 2% and accounted for nine recorded 2026 discoveries. Public Pool offers a zero-fee hosted option and accounts for five. Braiins Solo, which reportedly charges a 0.5% fee, is credited with five block discoveries this year.

Other choices include Atlaspool, Pool.bitaxe.de, Sololuck, Kanopool and Solopool.com. Some offer zero-fee arrangements, while others provide different server locations, mining protocols or payout structures.

The distinction becomes particularly important with hybrid services. Parasite Pool, for example, credited with five discoveries, has historically allocated a fixed 1 BTC to the finder and distributed the remainder among participating workers.

Nicehash Easymining offers another route through rented computing power rather than personally owned hardware. Meanwhile, P2Pool distributes rewards according to participating miners’ contributions, making it fundamentally different from winner-takes-all solo mining.

The Real Price of Chasing Bitcoin’s Jackpot

The attraction is obvious, but the economics remain unforgiving. At an assumed electricity rate of 15 cents per kilowatt-hour (kWh), a continuously operating 6 TH/s Avalon Nano 3S consumes approximately $184 annually in electricity.

You see, industrial-scale bitcoin miners often secure electricity rates of 7 cents per kilowatt-hour (kWh) or less, while ordinary households can pay considerably more, leaving everyday miners at a substantial economic disadvantage.

Using these assumptions, its probability-weighted annual reward is worth approximately $75 before pool fees and equipment expenses. A 1.2 TH/s Bitaxe produces an estimated $15 in annual expected rewards against roughly $26 in electricity costs.

These are statistical expectations, not dependable annual earnings. Most individual hobbyists receive nothing from genuine solo mining unless they discover a block. And that is precisely the kind of jackpot these everyday miners are hoping to hit.

For enthusiasts, the appeal therefore extends beyond conventional profitability. They are purchasing an opportunity, however improbable, to compete directly in Bitcoin’s block discovery process.

The Nov. 7 block height 974930 discovery captures that peculiar combination of engineering, astronomical odds, and extraordinary luck, where every hash is another roll of the dice in an ultimate lottery. Large operations possess overwhelming computational advantages, yet small machines can still participate in the same probabilistic contest. The odds favor the bitcoin mining giants, but the network’s lottery does not reserve every winning ticket for them.

title: IREN’s Bitcoin Mining Revenue Falls as AI Cloud Sales Nearly Triple
summary: IREN reported $200 million in quarterly AI Cloud revenue, up from $71 million the previous quarter, while Bitcoin mining revenue fell from $67 million to $28…
content:
TL;DR: IREN reported $200 million in quarterly AI Cloud revenue, up from $71 million the previous quarter, while Bitcoin mining revenue fell from $67 million to $28 million. Its November 5 results underline how quickly some former mining-led businesses are shifting towards AI infrastructure — and how expensive that shift remains.

IREN’s latest quarterly results offer a particularly stark view of the transition taking place across publicly listed Bitcoin infrastructure companies. A November 5 filing with the SEC reports $200 million of AI Cloud revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared with $71 million in the preceding quarter.

Bitcoin mining revenue, meanwhile, dropped to $28 million from $67 million. Total revenue rose to $228 million from $137 million, meaning the overall business expanded even as mining became a much smaller share of the total.

A different business is driving the growth

The company says AI Cloud revenue increased 182% sequentially and reported an 86% segment gross margin. That is a large change in a single quarter, supported by data-centre capacity coming online and customer contracts. But the term ‘gross margin’ is not a synonym for cash profit after financing, corporate expenses, depreciation and the capital needed to build the infrastructure.

IREN reported a net loss of $263 million for the September quarter, compared with a loss of $684 million in the preceding quarter. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $66 million from $19 million. The coexistence of strong revenue growth and a substantial accounting loss is precisely why neither metric should be read on its own.

The company said its revenue backlog increased to $20.3 billion, about two-thirds of it associated with investment-grade counterparties. A backlog is a contractual forward-looking figure subject to delivery schedules and contract terms; it is not cash already in the bank.

A timing change illustrates delivery risk

Management said a target of more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue is fully contracted and funded, but its timetable moved from the end of 2026 to January 2027 following a customer-requested design change and supplier timing. It said completion could extend into February. The distinction between contracted and operating capacity matters especially when large AI computing clusters depend on specialist components and commissioning schedules.

IREN highlighted the Horizon 1 facility entering service for Microsoft and said it had signed additional contracts after quarter-end. Its filing also described planned remaining fiscal-year capital spending and the financing it expects to use. Investors should compare the timing of expenditure with when customer payments are due rather than assuming a huge order book removes funding risks.

The trend resembles the shift described in NewsBTC’s wider examination of Bitcoin miners and AI infrastructure. However, each operator has its own contracting arrangements, retained mining fleet, power infrastructure and financial obligations.

Does a mining decline mean the network is weaker?

Not necessarily. IREN’s lower mining revenue tells us about one company’s business mix, not the aggregate computing power securing Bitcoin. Network difficulty, global hashrate and other miners’ decisions could move in different directions. NewsBTC’s reporting on hashrate competition is a useful counterpoint to the corporate story.

The next disclosures worth examining are realised AI revenue, actual data-centre commissioning, customer concentration, financing terms and remaining exposure to Bitcoin mining. IREN’s results show the transformation is already reflected in its income statement. Whether the economics produce durable shareholder returns depends on far more than the speed of this quarter’s revenue growth.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: TeraWulf Says AI Leasing Now Generates 83% of Revenue as Bitcoin Mining Recedes
summary: TeraWulf's November 6 earnings release shows $63 million in third-quarter high-performance-computing lease revenue, around 83% of its $76.2 million total.…
content:
TL;DR: TeraWulf’s November 6 earnings release shows $63 million in third-quarter high-performance-computing lease revenue, around 83% of its $76.2 million total. The company is increasingly an AI infrastructure business, although large non-cash gains and long-dated construction plans require careful reading.

TeraWulf is becoming a clear example of how the economics of Bitcoin mining can lead an infrastructure operator into a rather different business. In its third-quarter results published November 6, the Nasdaq-listed company said high-performance computing, or HPC, generated $63 million of lease revenue in the three months to September 30.

That represented about 83% of its $76.2 million quarterly revenue. Investors who still describe the firm primarily as a Bitcoin miner risk missing where its business is now concentrated and what its future costs may look like.

The revenue mix has already changed

The company operates existing mining infrastructure at its Lake Mariner campus but is repurposing portions of that site to support contracted computing workloads. TeraWulf said 102 megawatts of revenue-generating critical IT capacity were online at Lake Mariner at quarter-end, with another 336 megawatts under construction.

These numbers are not interchangeable with power agreements or theoretical campus capacity. A contract for future electricity or land does not mean an equivalent amount of paying data-centre capacity is already operating. The distinction matters when a company is projecting revenue from facilities that require years and significant capital to complete.

TeraWulf also reported net income of approximately $709.9 million for the quarter. But it attributed a significant benefit to a non-cash change in the fair value of warrants, while adjusted EBITDA was negative at about $12.8 million. That makes the headline profit a poor substitute for analysing recurring rental revenue, financing costs and operating cash flow.

Big contracts come with big execution demands

The company’s release described a 20-year Anthropic lease covering approximately 401 megawatts at its Justified development in Kentucky, representing around $19 billion in contracted revenue over the initial term. It also described a Google credit backstop supporting anticipated project financing and a definitive engineering, procurement and construction agreement with Fluor. These are material commercial commitments, not a claim that $19 billion has already been received.

TeraWulf expects phased service availability at Justified to begin in late 2027 and continue into 2028. At Muskie, it said contracted power capacity had expanded toward one gigawatt, subject to regulatory approval. Schedules, financing and utility infrastructure remain central risks.

NewsBTC has previously examined the mining industry’s move towards AI infrastructure. TeraWulf’s fresh results make that theme measurable: a majority of present revenue now comes from leases rather than mining.

Why this matters to Bitcoin markets

A miner switching to AI can reduce its exposure to Bitcoin production economics, including changes in difficulty, coin price and power cost. It can also create demand for the same grid connections, facilities and financing that historically supported mining. That transition need not be immediately positive or negative for Bitcoin’s network; it depends on which machines are retired, which are redeployed and whether remaining miners take up capacity.

The contrast with NewsBTC’s discussion of rising network hashrate is telling. Competition for mining rewards can intensify even while some large listed companies reshape themselves into computing landlords.

The milestones to watch are completed megawatts, actual rental commencement, capital spending against guidance, contractual counterparty exposure and cash generation. TeraWulf’s results show a dramatic change in revenue mix, but the hardest part of its next chapter will be delivering enormous physical projects reliably and profitably.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Bitcoin vs. Gold: Peter Schiff Highlights Strategy’s $75.5K Cost Basis and Missed 30% Return Target
summary: Peter Schiff has renewed his criticism of Bitcoin after Strategy's average purchase price moved close to the cryptocurrency's market value during the latest market pullback.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC XAU

Peter Schiff has renewed his criticism of Bitcoin after Strategy's average purchase price moved close to the cryptocurrency's market value during the latest market pullback.

The gold advocate used the development to question Michael Saylor’s six-year Bitcoin investment strategy, arguing that gold delivered substantially better returns over the same period. His comments have reignited the debate over BTC’s long-term performance compared with traditional precious metals.

According to Brave New Coin’s Bitcoin market data, BTC traded at approximately $75,955 on November 7, with a market capitalization of $1.5 trillion and 24-hour trading volume of $22.1 billion. The cryptocurrency was down 0.16% over 24 hours, 1.89% over seven days, and 8.62% over 30 days.

Strategy’s Bitcoin Holdings Return Close to Break-Even

Strategy’s Bitcoin treasury has moved close to its average acquisition cost as BTC trades around $75,955. The development follows a sharp market correction that erased a significant portion of BTC’s recent gains and placed the company’s accumulated holdings near break-even territory.

According to an SEC filing published November 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC as of November 1, following its latest purchase of 811 BTC for approximately $65.5 million. The company reported a cumulative acquisition cost of $64.08 billion, translating into an average purchase price of $75,451 per Bitcoin. The figures include fees and expenses.

Strategy acquired 811 BTC for $65 million, raising its total Bitcoin holdings to 849,327 BTC. Source: @BitcoinArchive via X

At the November 7 market price of $75,955, Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings were worth approximately $64.51 billion. This placed the company’s unrealized gain near $428 million, or roughly 0.67% above its aggregate acquisition cost. The margin remains relatively narrow given the size of its cryptocurrency position.

Strategy began accumulating BTC in August 2020, when the company, then operating as MicroStrategy, announced its initial purchase of 21,454 BTC for $250 million. The move established Bitcoin as its primary treasury reserve asset and eventually developed into one of the largest corporate cryptocurrency investment strategies.

Six years later, the company’s position has expanded considerably. However, BTC’s return toward Strategy’s average acquisition price has given critics an opportunity to question the results of its long-term accumulation approach.

The latest figures follow another round of purchases in October, continuing a strategy that has relied on equity offerings and other financing arrangements to expand its Bitcoin treasury. Brave New Coin’s previous coverage of Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation provides additional context on how the company has continued increasing its holdings.

Schiff Challenges Saylor’s 30% Annual Bitcoin Return Outlook

Schiff used a sarcastic message on X to congratulate Bitcoin supporters as Strategy’s average purchase price approached the market rate. His criticism focused on the difference between Saylor’s bullish long-term expectations and the relatively narrow unrealized gain on the company’s Bitcoin holdings.

Schiff argues gold would have doubled investors’ money, while Strategy’s promised 30% annual Bitcoin returns have fallen short. Source: Peter Schiff via X

A central part of the debate involves Saylor’s expectation that BTC could appreciate approximately 30% annually over an extended period. During a December 19, 2025, CoinDesk interview, the Strategy executive chairman stated, “I expect Bitcoin will appreciate about 30% a year for the next 20 years.”

The statement reflected Saylor’s long-term outlook for Bitcoin rather than a guaranteed return or a specific annual performance commitment by Strategy. Nevertheless, Schiff used the company’s position near its average cost basis to challenge the investment thesis behind years of continued accumulation.

The distinction between BTC’s market performance and Strategy’s overall investment returns is also important. The company’s average acquisition price represents the weighted cost of its Bitcoin holdings, not the return generated by its publicly traded shares. Strategy’s financing arrangements, share issuance, debt obligations, and other capital costs also influence shareholder outcomes.

Consequently, BTC trading close to the company’s average purchase price does not independently establish the total performance of Strategy’s investment strategy. It does, however, highlight how quickly the value of a substantial corporate Bitcoin treasury can change during market corrections.

Gold Performance Fuels Schiff’s Bitcoin Criticism

Schiff also revived his longstanding argument that gold has been a better investment than Bitcoin over the comparison period. He suggested that investors would have roughly doubled their money by choosing the precious metal instead of following Saylor’s cryptocurrency strategy.

The chart compares gold’s historical cycles since 2010, highlighting similar rebounds near the 100- and 200-month moving averages and projected upside targets of $4,800–$5,000. Source: @TradingShot via X

Historical pricing provides context for the comparison. Gold closed near $1,915.79 per ounce on August 11, 2020, when MicroStrategy announced its initial BTC purchase. By November 6, 2026, gold had reached approximately $4,070.59, representing an increase of around 112.5%.

However, the comparison requires additional context. BTC closed near $11,410.53 on August 11, 2020, and traded around $75,955 on November 7, 2026. That represents an increase of approximately 566% over the same period.

These figures compare the market prices of the two assets, not the returns generated by Strategy’s entire investment portfolio. Its $75,451 average purchase price reflects hundreds of transactions made at different market levels over six years, rather than a single investment made in August 2020.

This distinction is important when assessing Schiff’s argument. Gold has more than doubled since Strategy announced its initial Bitcoin investment, but Bitcoin’s market price has also appreciated substantially. Strategy’s relatively narrow unrealized gain reflects the company’s cumulative buying prices, not BTC’s overall performance since 2020.

Gold and Bitcoin also have different market characteristics. Gold has an established history as a monetary and investment asset, while BTC operates as a decentralized digital asset with a comparatively shorter market history. Both can experience substantial price fluctuations, and neither guarantees positive returns.

Schiff has consistently favored precious metals over cryptocurrencies, frequently questioning BTC’s ability to maintain its value over extended periods. His latest criticism follows that established position, with Strategy’s near-break-even valuation providing a fresh point of comparison.

For additional context on recent precious metals performance, Brave New Coin’s latest gold price forecast examines bullion’s movements around the $4,000 level and the potential influence of Federal Reserve policy.

US Midterm Elections Add a Political Dimension to Bitcoin’s Weakness

Schiff’s criticism has also extended beyond investment performance. Following the November 3, 2026, US midterm elections, he connected BTC’s declining price with the political position of President Donald Trump, whom he described as “the Bitcoin president.”

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, according to the Associated Press. The outcome represents a shift in the political balance ahead of the new Congress taking office in January 2027. Schiff framed the result as a rejection of Trump’s political standing and argued that it could weaken the administration’s influence over cryptocurrency policy.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

In his commentary, Schiff reinforced the relationship he sees between Trump’s political fortunes and Bitcoin’s market performance. His argument reflects his longstanding criticism of the cryptocurrency and support for gold rather than independently established evidence that political developments determine BTC’s direction.

BTC experienced significant volatility around the election results. The cryptocurrency briefly fell below $76,000 on November 3 before recovering toward $78,000 the following day. However, the recovery failed to establish a sustained move above $80,000, leaving the market vulnerable to another round of selling.

The broader financial environment also contributed to uncertainty. Weakness in technology stocks, changes in investor risk appetite, and fluctuations in institutional cryptocurrency demand have added pressure to digital assets.

Brave New Coin’s coverage of Bitcoin’s reaction to the 2026 US midterm elections examines the initial selloff, subsequent recovery, and changing spot-market demand.

For now, Strategy’s Bitcoin position remains close to its aggregate acquisition cost, while Schiff continues to use gold’s performance to challenge Saylor’s investment thesis. The next phase of Bitcoin’s market performance will determine whether the company can rebuild a wider unrealized gain or faces renewed pressure on its substantial treasury position.
