title: Prediction Markets Favor Another Drop as Year-End Bitcoin Price Forecasts Sour
summary: Bitcoin price prediction markets are signaling a difficult finish to 2026, with Polymarket traders assigning a 52% probability to a $70,000 retreat before January and just 9% to a $100,000 comeback, while Kalshi participants concentrate their year-end expectations around $70,000 to $80,000. As of no...
content:
Bitcoin price prediction markets are signaling a difficult finish to 2026, with Polymarket traders assigning a 52% probability to a $70,000 retreat before January and just 9% to a $100,000 comeback, while Kalshi participants concentrate their year-end expectations around $70,000 to $80,000.

Key Takeaways

  • Polymarket traders assign a 52% probability to bitcoin’s price touching $70,000 before 2027, compared with 24% for $90,000.
  • Kalshi’s two leading year-end price brackets carry a combined 35.1% implied probability.
  • November contracts favor a test of $72,500 over a return to $90,000, although prices and probabilities vary across platforms.

As of noon Eastern time on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, bitcoin’s price traded at $75,723, down 2.4% over seven days and 6.6% over the preceding month. With fewer than eight weeks remaining in the calendar year, prediction markets reveal considerable skepticism about a meaningful recovery.

Across prediction marketplaces like Polymarket, Kalshi, and Myriad, traders are positioning around lower price thresholds while assigning increasingly remote probabilities to six-figure valuations. The figures reflect market-implied expectations rather than definitive forecasts, and the differences between contract structures deserve particular attention.

Polymarket Traders See $70,000 as the Next Major Test

Polymarket’s 2026 bitcoin price market has accumulated approximately $82.74 million in trading volume across more than 46 price targets. Its most probable unresolved outcome is a decline to $70,000, carrying a 52% implied probability.

A deeper retreat to $65,000 commands 31%, while $60,000 carries 18%. The probabilities diminish considerably beyond those levels, with $55,000 priced at 11% and $50,000 at 6%.

Conversely, bitcoin’s price reaching $90,000 before year’s end carries only a 24% probability. That figure declines to 13% at $95,000 and 9% at $100,000. The market places just 3% on $120,000, while $150,000 commands approximately 2%.

These contracts measure whether bitcoin’s price touches a designated value, not where it finishes the year. Consequently, multiple thresholds can resolve successfully during the same period, making their probabilities fundamentally different from mutually exclusive closing-price predictions.

Kalshi Traders Cluster Around $75,000

Kalshi’s year-end bitcoin price market presents another perspective, with approximately $46.01 million in cumulative volume. Unlike Polymarket’s threshold contracts, Kalshi’s year-end ranges identify where bitcoin will settle when 2026 concludes.

The $75,000 to $79,999.99 bracket leads with a 17.6% probability, narrowly ahead of $70,000 to $74,999.99 at 17.5%. The $80,000 to $84,999.99 range follows at 12.5%.

Together, the two leading brackets account for 35.1% of implied probability, illustrating the concentration around bitcoin’s prevailing valuation. Nevertheless, their combined probability also leaves considerable room for outcomes outside that corridor.

Kalshi determines settlement using the CME CF Bitcoin Real Time Index, averaging 60 consecutive one-second observations during the final minute of Dec. 31. That methodology differs from Polymarket’s Binance-based intraday threshold measurements.

What Are Traders Expecting Before November Ends?

The shorter November contracts offer an equally revealing picture. Polymarket assigns an 81% probability to bitcoin touching $77,500 and 56% to $80,000 before December.

However, those expectations deteriorate at higher thresholds. A move to $85,000 carries 23%, while $90,000 commands just 9%. Reaching $100,000 during November is priced at approximately 1%.

Downside expectations tell a different story. Traders assign 61% to bitcoin touching $72,500, 43% to $70,000 and 26% to $67,500.

Kalshi’s November high-price contracts broadly reflect this caution. Its market assigns 35% to exceeding $82,500, 21% to $85,000 and 15% to $87,500, with approximately $982,199 in cumulative trading volume.

Meanwhile, Myriad displays similar November probabilities, but its trading activity is extraordinarily thin compared to the two aforementioned prediction marketplace giants. Its upside market has recorded approximately $96 in volume, while its downside counterpart has attracted a measly $5.68 in trade volume.

Such modest participation makes Myriad’s quotations extremely poor independent evidence of market consensus, regardless of how closely they resemble prices on larger platforms.

Still, taking the extremely limited participation into account, Myriad’s November markets assign bitcoin a 43% chance of falling to $70,000, a 61% probability of touching $72,500, and just a 9% likelihood of reaching $90,000.

A Narrowing Window for Bitcoin’s Bulls

The distinction between expectations and outcomes remains essential. Prediction-market prices reflect what participants are willing to pay for specific contracts, not a statistically guaranteed probability of future price movements.

Nevertheless, the prevailing message is difficult to overlook. Prediction event traders currently regard another visit to $70,000 as considerably more plausible than a return to $100,000 before January.

The remaining weeks of 2026 will determine whether that caution proves justified. For now, the most revealing development is not simply the market’s preference for lower prices, but the increasingly expensive proposition of betting against its prevailing pessimism.

title: Binance Hack Takes Another Twist as Hackers Amass 2,300 More Bitcoin
summary: In the aftermath of the colossal $6.3 billion Binance hack, which saw 18,270.2 BTC drained from the crypto exchange’s wallet, onchain intelligence and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic has revealed that the attacker’s bitcoin holdings are growing considerably larger. According to Elliptic, the hack...
content:
In the aftermath of the colossal $6.3 billion Binance hack, which saw 18,270.2 BTC drained from the crypto exchange’s wallet, onchain intelligence and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic has revealed that the attacker’s bitcoin holdings are growing considerably larger. According to Elliptic, the hackers have converted $175 million in stolen altcoins into approximately 2,300 BTC, further expanding their bitcoin reserves.

Key Takeaways

  • The bitcoin conversion: Hackers transformed $175 million in stolen altcoins into 2,300 BTC, according to Elliptic.
  • The vanishing trail: Over 20,000 wallets and 65,000 transactions obscure the stolen funds.
  • The untouched fortune: The hackers’ primary bitcoin and ethereum holdings remain dormant.

How Did Binance Hackers Turn Stolen Altcoins Into 2,300 BTC?

The Oct. 29, 2026, Binance hack stands as the largest cryptocurrency exchange breach in U.S. dollar terms, with the attackers making off with an extraordinary haul. Last week, Bitcoin.com News detailed how the perpetrators siphoned 18,270.2 BTC from the trading platform, while onchain records and blockchain forensic analysts now indicate that their bitcoin stockpile is growing considerably larger.

This week, Elliptic co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Tom Robinson published a detailed examination of the incident, incorporating updates through Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Robinson’s findings reveal that altcoins stolen during the Binance breach have since been converted into approximately 2,300 BTC, valued at $175 million based on bitcoin prices as of Nov. 7.

“The laundering is highly complex and clearly automated,” Robinson’s report details. “Since the theft it has used more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions. That is roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds.”

From Solana to Bitcoin, a Multichain Laundering Operation

The Elliptic co-founder detailed how the attackers transferred approximately $90 million in stolen solana (SOL), with much of the proceeds ultimately converted into bitcoin. XRP also emerged as a substantial contributor to the attackers’ expanding bitcoin holdings, while stolen tron (TRX) was similarly exchanged for BTC.

Ethereum (ETH) accounted for a smaller portion of the conversions, while the attackers also employed Thorchain to facilitate cross-chain asset swaps. Throughout Robinson’s analysis, the Elliptic boss repeatedly ties the hackers to North Korea, and the country is mentioned eight times.

How Are the Hackers Obscuring Their Bitcoin Trail?

A portion of the newly acquired bitcoin subsequently flowed through Wasabi Wallet coinjoins, a transaction technique that commingles bitcoin from multiple participants to complicate blockchain tracing efforts. By Nov. 7, Robinson’s analysis indicated that approximately 88 BTC, valued at $6.7 million, had been processed through this obfuscation method.

The Elliptic co-founder further noted:

“On NEAR, approximately 412,000 NEAR ($1.5 million) left the main accounts in small batches. In total, roughly 2,300 BTC ($175 million) now sit in newly created bitcoin addresses following conversions from other stolen cryptocurrencies. Meanwhile, the primary bitcoin and ETH holdings remain untouched.”

At the same time, data gathered by Bitcoin.com News from blockchain analytics platform Arkham Intelligence paints a somewhat different picture, showing no corresponding addition of 2,300 BTC, although the original 18,270.2 BTC attributed to the attackers had climbed to 18,384.725 BTC as of 10 a.m. ET on Nov. 7, 2026.

Arkham’s transaction records nevertheless reveal bitcoin deposits originating from Thorchain vaults on Saturday, alongside TRX token swaps executed through Sun.io, a prominent decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol operating on the Tron network.

title: Microsoft Faces AI Backlash as 100+ Protesters Break Into $1B Amsterdam Data Center Project
summary: More than 100 activists broke into a Microsoft-linked data center construction site in Amsterdam on November 6, climbing cranes and displaying banners against the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure.
content:
Skip to content

More than 100 activists broke into a Microsoft-linked data center construction site in Amsterdam on November 6, climbing cranes and displaying banners against the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The demonstration brought together environmental campaigners and other protest groups concerned about the industry’s growing demand for electricity, water, and land. Police intervened and detained between 150 and 200 people on suspicion of trespassing, according to Dutch authorities.

Protesters Target Microsoft Data Center Construction Site

The demonstration took place at a construction site in Amsterdam’s Westpoort district, where Pure Data Centers is developing a facility intended for Microsoft. Members of the Dutch activist group Geef Tegengas entered the site, climbed construction structures and a crane, and displayed banners criticizing artificial intelligence and Microsoft’s business activities.

Reuters footage shows around 100 activists breaching a Microsoft data center construction site near Amsterdam on November 6, 2026, protesting the facility’s development. Source: Reuters via X

Footage from the scene showed protesters scaling fences, gathering around construction equipment, and displaying messages including “Fuck AI” and “Microsoft Powered Genocide.” Some demonstrators also set off flares and spray-painted slogans around the site. The action drew attention to both the environmental impact of data center expansion and concerns about the use of Microsoft’s technology in military and surveillance operations.

Sam van der Beek, a protester involved in the demonstration, told Reuters that data centers were “destroying our world” because of the resources they consume. He added that the growing environmental burden was making the planet increasingly difficult to inhabit.

The protest also involved groups opposing Microsoft’s connections to military and government surveillance operations. Demonstrators displayed Palestinian flags and banners criticizing the company’s services to the Israeli military and the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. These concerns added a human rights dimension to the wider opposition against AI infrastructure.

Police moved to clear the construction site as tensions increased. The Associated Press reported that some activists clashed with officers, while DutchNews reported the use of pepper spray. Dutch police later confirmed that between 150 and 200 people had been detained on suspicion of trespassing. An officer also sustained a minor injury during the demonstration, according to a police statement reported by The Guardian.

Energy and Water Consumption Drive Opposition

Environmental concerns remain at the center of the growing resistance to AI data centers across Europe. Campaigners argue that facilities supporting cloud computing and artificial intelligence require substantial electricity, cooling resources, and land, potentially placing additional pressure on communities already dealing with infrastructure constraints.

Protester Sam van der Beek criticized data centers for their heavy consumption of water, electricity, and land, while the action formed part of a Europe-wide campaign calling for construction to be halted. Source: The Washington Post via X

The Amsterdam project has attracted particular attention because of its expected electricity demand. According to information published by Pure Data Centers, the Westpoort campus will have three towers with a combined data hall capacity of 78 megawatts (MW). The developer plans to connect the facility to the electricity grid through a dedicated substation.

The project’s scale has raised questions about how new data centers will compete with households, businesses, and other developments for limited power resources. The Netherlands is already dealing with electricity grid congestion, creating challenges for companies seeking new or upgraded connections. Campaigners argue that allocating substantial capacity to AI infrastructure could make it harder to accommodate other local priorities.

Water consumption is another concern. Data centers require cooling systems to maintain operating temperatures, with demand depending on the technology and cooling methods used. Activists fear that a rapid increase in computing facilities could put additional pressure on local water supplies and environmental resources.

The campaign also challenges the concentration of digital infrastructure within a small number of technology companies. Protesters argue that decisions about where facilities are built and how they operate should involve greater public consultation, particularly when local communities may experience the environmental and infrastructure costs.

$1B Microsoft Data Center Project Raises Regulatory Questions

Pure Data Centers plans to invest more than €1 billion in the Amsterdam Westpoort campus, which is fully leased to Microsoft. The development will consist of three towers, each approximately 85 meters tall, across a site covering around six acres.

The developer estimates that construction and related activities will directly provide more than 1,000 jobs. Once operational, the campus is expected to support approximately 80 permanent positions involving engineering, maintenance, security, and administration.

Electricity requirements remain a central issue in the debate. A Dutch government response to parliamentary questions published in April 2026 stated that the project’s grid connection capacity would reach 99 MW, based on 33 MW for each tower. The government calculated that continuous electricity demand at that level would amount to approximately 0.87 terawatt-hours (TWh) annually.

That figure represents a theoretical calculation based on continuous full-capacity consumption rather than verified annual usage. The distinction is important when assessing the project’s expected impact on the local power network.

The government also noted that the development would not use groundwater following discussions with the developer. The project was also designed to transfer heat to a planned heating facility across the street, providing a potential use for some of the heat generated during operations.

Amsterdam Data Center Restrictions and Project Approval

The development has also drawn scrutiny because Amsterdam has introduced restrictions on new data center construction. In April 2025, the city barred new data centers and expansions within the municipality until at least 2030, citing concerns over electricity demand and the pressure placed on local resources.

However, the Microsoft-linked project has a longer regulatory history. According to the Dutch government’s response to parliamentary questions, the original building permit was requested in December 2019 and granted on November 6, 2020, before the national restrictions on hyperscale data centers took effect.

The national rules, introduced in January 2024, restrict new hyperscale facilities based on specific size and electricity connection thresholds. The government’s definition covers projects with more than 10 hectares of built floor space and an electricity connection capacity of at least 70 MW.

Officials said the Amsterdam development does not fall within that legal definition because its built floor area remains below the 10-hectare threshold. The government’s explanation indicates that the project’s earlier approval and legal classification allowed it to proceed despite subsequent restrictions on large-scale data center development.

The regulatory history has not ended public criticism. Environmental organizations and local campaigners continue to question whether existing approval processes adequately account for electricity demand, land use, and the long-term effects of AI infrastructure on surrounding communities.

Microsoft and Pure Data Centers Respond

Microsoft acknowledged the demonstration and defended the right of people to express their concerns peacefully. However, the company opposed the protesters’ entry into the construction site.

“We understand that people feel strongly about the project, and we respect their right to express those views peacefully,” a Microsoft spokesperson said. “However, we do not condone any actions that are unlawful or that put people’s safety at risk.”

Pure Data Centers also called on demonstrators to leave the site safely and offered to discuss their concerns. The company said it remained committed to engaging with local stakeholders and emphasized the importance of maintaining safety at an active construction site.

The developer’s position reflects the wider infrastructure industry’s argument that data centers provide essential computing capacity for businesses, governments, and consumers. Technology companies consider these facilities necessary to support cloud services, AI applications, and the growing demand for digital processing.

European Opposition to AI Data Center Expansion Grows

The Amsterdam demonstration coincided with the November 6-7 European action days organized by the Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition. The campaign brings together environmental organizations, digital rights groups, and community movements calling for a temporary halt to new large-scale data center construction until stronger environmental and regulatory safeguards are established.

Data centers’ water-intensive cooling systems and land-clearing requirements can reduce local freshwater availability and disrupt natural water cycles. Source: Sharon Collins via X

Campaigners organized demonstrations in several countries, including Germany, Poland, Ireland, Italy, and the United Kingdom. Their demands include greater transparency, more public involvement in planning decisions, and clearer requirements for electricity and water consumption.

The campaign has also highlighted concerns about whether the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is compatible with Europe’s climate objectives. Data centers are becoming an increasingly important part of the region’s digital economy, but their growing energy requirements have prompted questions about grid capacity and the availability of renewable electricity.

European policymakers face the challenge of expanding computing infrastructure while protecting consumers and local communities from additional environmental and energy pressures. EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen has argued that Europe needs more data centers to develop its own AI capacity while warning that expansion must not drive up electricity bills, increase the risk of power shortages, or damage the environment.

The Amsterdam protest illustrates how these competing priorities are becoming increasingly difficult to reconcile. With Microsoft-linked construction continuing despite local opposition, the debate over AI infrastructure is moving beyond technology investment and into questions of environmental responsibility, public oversight, and corporate accountability.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, the US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities, the Treasury also moved to cut MEXC off from the US financial system over alleged illicit transactions, and questions remain about Binance’s hot wallet safeguards following its $6.3 billion hack.

US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties

The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities.

These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday.

The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US.

These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury.

US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

The US Department of Treasury on Friday issued an order to cut cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global off from the US’ financial system after accusing it of facilitating at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, cybercrime and other illicit activity.

The Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) asserted that MEXC handled transactions involving sanctioned groups in Iran, Russia and North Korea between May 2021 and May 2026. This included around $1.5 billion in transactions linked to Russian sanctions evasion, according to the official press release.

The order effectively bans US financial institutions from processing money transfers involving MEXC and will take effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register. 

“Financial institutions cannot have it both ways: Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will continue to sever the Iranian regime’s economic lifelines and thwart its desperate attempts to circumvent U.S. sanctions using digital assets.”

The action is part of Operation Economic Outcast, a US Treasury campaign launched in August with aims to cut off financial entities that help Iran evade sanctions.

According to DefiLlama, the exchange held about $4.48 billion in total assets as of Friday. Cointelegraph contacted MEXC for comment but had not received a response by publication.

Binance’s $6.3B hack leaves questions over hot wallet safeguards

Binance’s $6.3 billion security incident has left unanswered questions about how the exchange managed its hot wallets and limited the amount attackers could access.

Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on Oct. 30 that the attack affected the exchange’s own hot wallet. Most customer assets were held in offline cold storage and moved to hot wallets only when users requested withdrawals.

Wallet balances offer only a partial picture of an exchange’s exposure to an attack. Public blockchain records can show funds moving but cannot establish the internal controls governing those transfers, CertiK analyst Jonathan Riss told Cointelegraph.

In its initial report Tuesday, Binance said attackers accessed an internal wallet-signing service to move funds outside its normal withdrawal process. Binance said some technical details would remain confidential to prevent further attacks.

title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
summary: Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard.
content:
A former FBI counterintelligence agent admitted to wire fraud and money laundering in stealing almost $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from unidentified adversarial nations and wallets that were under investigation.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, used his investigative positions with access to FBI systems to steal cryptocurrency, then exchange and launder it through financial transactions to conceal its source and ownership.

Yaroch made about 100 fraudulent transfers related to 35 FBI investigations, gaining $2,474,380.66 in proceeds, according to a news release from the US Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Virginia on Thursday.

He had earlier admitted to unauthorized transfers that involved about $1 million in digital assets, which was reported by Cointelegraph in August.

Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard, according to the statement.

The former agent admitted that his actions had compromised FBI investigations related to criminal groups and adversarial nations. 

Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison. His sentencing is set for March 4, 2027.

title: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?
summary: Bitcoin’s eCash fork gives eligible holders an equivalent balance of ECX, but questions remain over where they can trade the tokens and what they can do with them.
content:
Somewhere between the Binance hack and the US midterms, Paul Sztorc’s long-awaited Bitcoin fork, known as the eCash network, went live.

On Oct. 29, Sztorc, the founder of LayerTwo Labs and the driving force behind the Bitcoin Drivechain proposals BIP300 and BIP301 , launched a separate Bitcoin fork designed to bring payments, privacy and other applications to a network built from Bitcoin’s code.

“We need to actively sabotage the ‘degrowth’ policies killing Bitcoin,” Sztorc tells Magazine.

“We want to find the true Bitcoin builders and give them the tools to actually innovate. We just need the open-minded, risk-taking contrarians to come and build.”

The hard fork gives eligible Bitcoin holders an interesting windfall: their equivalent BTC balance in the new chain’s native token, ECX.

So what benefits does eCash bring to developers, and what can Bitcoin HODLers actually do with their new coins?

What is eCash?

Developed by Sztorc’s LayerTwo Labs, eCash is a separate hard fork of Bitcoin born out of Sztorc’s frustration with some of the “complacency narratives” and “cult-like toxicity” he believes has been holding Bitcoin back.

Sztorc dismisses criticism of Drivechains’ security. Source: archive.ecash

Its main innovation is Drivechains, a system that gives developers freedom to build independent sidechains with different features without having to make changes to Bitcoin’s base-layer protocol (or in this case, eCash’s base layer).

Developers can experiment with different applications for payments, privacy, digital assets and prediction markets, and miners can “maximize their revenues” by earning additional transaction fees.

Five sidechains launched alongside eCash’s mainnet: BitNames, BitAssets, Thunder, Truthcoin and zSide, with two more, the quantum-resistant Photon and decentralized exchange CoinShift, still to come.

Related: Blockchain developer Paul Sztorc announces BTC hard fork eCash

Sztorc has spent over a decade advocating for Drivechains and believes that Bitcoin’s notoriously conservative development approach has held back its potential.

“Anything that isn’t maximizing network usage is simply a distraction,” he says. “Users, the ones who actually pay transaction fees to miners, will win in the long run.”

Getting access to the new coins

The eCash fork took place at Bitcoin block 973,728, and anyone who controlled their private keys at the snapshot received an equivalent ECX balance.

“If you held the keys to your BTC at that exact block, you now own the exact same amount of ECX,” LayerTwo Labs tells Magazine. “It is that simple, and you can access them right now.”

Like beauty, simplicity is in the eye of the beholder, and Bitcoiners who self-custody their coins will need to use a wallet that supports eCash and carefully follow its process to separate the ECX from their BTC.

Because the two networks share transaction history, an unprotected transaction on one chain could be replayed on the other.

eCash Market prices. Source: eCash.

“Never move your BTC first, as an ordinary, unprotected BTC spend can easily be replayed on the ECX network,” LayerTwo Labs warns. Replay controls are built into the protocol, it says, but the company advises holders to move ECX first, before spending BTC.

Anyone keeping BTC on a centralized exchange is “at their mercy regarding distribution,” and should check whether their exchange supports the fork or has announced an ECX distribution.

Where can holders trade ECX?

Accessing ECX isn’t the same thing as being able to sell it and the tokens are not yet widely available on larger crypto exchanges. Depending on which country you are in, there can be tax implications from Bitcoin forks, which are worth looking up before filing your next tax return.

NeoxEX said it opened native ECX deposits, withdrawals and trading on Oct. 29, with ECX/USDT, ECX/USDC and ECX/BTC pairs, while CoinW announced plans to distribute ECX to eligible Bitcoin holders, with deposits, withdrawals and trading to be announced at a later date.

Orca, a decentralized exchange on Solana, lets users swap USDC for wrapped ECX (wECX) through a liquidity pool. That gives holders another way to trade exposure to ECX, but it involves a wrapped token on a different blockchain rather than native ECX trading on the eCash network.

Related: Binance, Polymarket seek Polygon hard fork to recover $6.8M in stolen crypto

How much are the tokens worth? CoinMarketCap placed ECX at $32.63, with around $355,000 in 24-hour trading volume as of Nov. 5, while CoinGecko shows the token as a preview listing, with no price yet available and no tracked exchange markets. Crypto market data provider Kaiko says it does not track ECX, which limits the availability of independent market data.

LayerTwo Labs says early trading saw ECX fluctuate between $40 and $50, but it did not provide supporting order book depth or trading volume figures, pointing instead to the Orca pool’s total value locked as a way for users to assess available liquidity.

eCash is $32.63 on CoinMarketCap as of Nov. 5

“If our fork replicates even a fraction of [Bitcoin Cash] BCH’s initial performance,” Sztorc says, “the liquidity will be staggering,” adding that anyone concerned about low liquidity can hold their coins and decide later.

“We are actively adding new exchanges and trading pairs, so the user experience will only improve,” he says. “Otherwise, you’re welcome to take your free money and leave.”

A different vision for Bitcoin

Sztorc says the value of eCash will ultimately depend on whether developers build useful applications and users are willing to pay for them. Paying customers and transaction fee revenue are the project’s main measures of success during its first year, he says.

He’s not concerned about criticism of Drivechains’ security model, especially the “superstition” that miners could coordinate to steal funds held on sidechains.

“If you genuinely believe miners will torch their own billion-dollar operations for a short-term theft on an L2, then you shouldn’t trust Bitcoin’s L1 either,” he says.

So for now, eCash gives Bitcoiners a new asset and developers a new playground — but whether ECX becomes much more than that will depend on whether anyone actually wants to use it.

title: US sanctions Canadian money-exchange firms over Iran ties
summary: US  also offers as much as $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program.
content:
The US Treasury imposed financial sanctions on eight Canadian money-service companies it claims have done business with sanctioned ‌Iranian entities.

These companies facilitated the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, enabling international transactions, a US Treasury Department statement said on Friday.

The sanctions, which serve to isolate the companies from the dollar-based financial system, are the latest in a series of Treasury moves against firms outside the US.

These businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), according to the Treasury.

Bessent says Canada cannot be a safe haven

Related: US plans to seize $1B in crypto linked to Iran this week: Scott Bessent

“Canada cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators that provide sanctions evasion services to the Iranian regime and its proxies,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury will pursue and disrupt the Iranian regime’s financial channels anywhere in the world.”

Cointelegraph reported in August that the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control, or OFAC, was targeting crypto exchanges facilitating the transfer of funds to Iran’s IRGC. Bessent said at the time that the US planned to “increase the economic pressure” on Iran, focusing on financial networks funding the country’s regime “in dollars, rials, or crypto.”

Friday’s designations are a continuation of Treasury’s campaign to “disrupt the regime’s exploitation of digital assets to fund terrorism, human rights abuses, and attacks on US personnel and allies,” the statement said.

It added that the actions were coordinated with FINTRAC, Canada’s financial intelligence unit.  

Some of the entities subject to this action have changed their names and addresses to evade detection, the statement noted.

Reward of $20 million for Iran nuclear information

In a separate action on Friday, the US Rewards for Justice program offered as much as $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment and personnel.

Iran’s lack of compliance with the International Atomic Energy Agency on safeguards has led to the agency’s loss of “continuity of knowledge” regarding Iran’s production of enriched uranium and components like centrifuges, the statement said.

title: BNB Price Prediction: $690 Make-or-Break Retest Could Decide Between $1,400 Rally and $290 Crash
summary: BNB is trading near $690 as conflicting Elliott Wave projections and bearish chart patterns put its recent macro breakout under pressure.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BNB

BNB is trading near $690 as conflicting Elliott Wave projections and bearish chart patterns put its recent macro breakout under pressure.

The $690–$700 region has emerged as a critical retest zone, with analysts watching whether buyers can defend the level or allow a deeper correction.

BNB price remains above its 200-day moving average, suggesting that its longer-term market structure has not completely deteriorated. However, negative MACD momentum and resistance from shorter-term moving averages indicate that a sustained recovery has yet to materialize.

BNB Faces a Critical $690 Retest as Elliott Wave Scenarios Diverge

BNB is approaching an important technical decision point after retreating from its late-October highs near $750. The cryptocurrency was trading around $694–$696 in early November 2026, with recent sessions showing a modest recovery from lows near $684–$687.

BNB is retesting a critical weekly support zone after breaking its macro range, with the outcome likely to determine its next major price move. Source: @MarzellCrypto via X

The current price area aligns with a weekly breakout retest identified by crypto analyst @MarzellCrypto. In a November 3 analysis, the trader described the region as a “make-or-break” level that could determine BNB’s next major directional move.

The bullish scenario depends on buyers defending the former macro resistance area as support. If the retest holds, the previous breakout structure could remain intact, keeping the possibility of new all-time highs open. However, a sustained loss of support could expose BNB to lower price levels around $365 and potentially $290.

Despite outlining these downside risks, MarzellCrypto maintains a bullish bias while the breakout zone remains defended. The distinction is important because a successful retest would indicate that buyers are still willing to accumulate near the former resistance level.

The bullish setup remains intact unless BNB records a weekly close above $813, with a successful hold of the lower support zone potentially paving the way for a rally above $1,400. Source: @WhaleFactor via X

A separate analysis from WhaleFactor presents a considerably deeper corrective scenario. Its weekly Elliott Wave count identifies an ABC correction following a rally of approximately 580%, which carried BNB to a peak near $1,173.

According to the analysis, Wave B encountered rejection around $813, leaving the token exposed to a potential Wave C decline. WhaleFactor identifies a broad completion zone between $398 and $310, where a longer-term bottoming structure could develop.

The analyst’s projected bearish count remains valid unless BNB records a weekly close above $813. If the projected correction eventually reaches its lower target zone and buying interest returns, the next potential impulse wave could carry the asset above $1,400.

These projections represent separate technical scenarios rather than confirmed price outcomes. The $290–$398 region reflects the deeper downside estimates, while the $1,400 target depends on a successful corrective bottom and subsequent bullish reversal.

Head and Shoulders Pattern Adds to BNB’s Bearish Technical Outlook

Shorter-term chart signals are adding another layer of uncertainty to BNB’s recovery attempt. TradingView analyst DamonEdge has identified a bearish Head and Shoulders formation on the daily BNB/USDT chart, suggesting that selling pressure may continue if the token fails to reclaim its broken neckline.

BNB’s break below the neckline and failed recovery reinforce the bearish outlook, with further downside toward $625 expected if the price remains below this level. Source: DamonEdge on TradingView

The pattern consists of three peaks, with the middle peak forming the head and the two surrounding peaks creating the shoulders. In this case, the right shoulder failed to reach the height of the head, indicating weakening buying pressure during the recovery attempt.

More importantly, BNB has already moved below the neckline. The subsequent rebound also failed to establish a sustained recovery above that level, strengthening the bearish interpretation of the formation.

DamonEdge identified $625 as the next downside target if the breakdown remains intact. The analyst stated, “As long as BNB remains below the broken neckline, I expect selling pressure to continue.”

This projection introduces another downside level between the current trading range and the deeper targets identified by MarzellCrypto and WhaleFactor. A move toward $625 would represent an initial test of bearish momentum rather than confirmation of a broader breakdown toward $365 or $290.

However, a recovery above the neckline could weaken the pattern’s bearish implications. Traders would need to monitor whether BNB can establish sustained buying interest rather than relying on a brief rebound.

BNB Technical Indicators Show Weak Momentum Below Key Moving Averages

Daily technical indicators present a mixed picture, with shorter-term signals favoring sellers while the longer-term structure remains comparatively stable.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is hovering around 40–41, indicating weak momentum without reaching the conventional oversold threshold of 30. This suggests that selling pressure remains present, although the indicator does not yet confirm an extreme downside condition.

BNB price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) also remains negative. Its MACD line is positioned around -12.3 to -12.6, below the signal line near -9.6 to -10.1. The negative histogram indicates that bearish momentum has not fully subsided.

Other indicators offer some evidence of short-term stabilization. The Stochastic oscillator has moved into lower territory, while the Commodity Channel Index (CCI), near -100 to -111, indicates that BNB could be approaching levels associated with potential mean reversion.

However, these readings do not independently establish a bullish reversal.

Moving averages provide a clearer picture of the current resistance structure. BNB remains below its 10-day, 20-day, 30-day, and 50-day moving averages, which are clustered between approximately $702 and $746. The 50-day simple moving average near $746 represents a particularly important recovery hurdle.

In contrast, the 200-day simple moving average remains near $657, below the current market price. This indicates that BNB has retained an important element of its longer-term bullish structure despite its recent decline.

For a stronger recovery signal, BNB would need to reclaim the $710–$722 resistance region. A MACD crossover above its signal line and an RSI move above 50 would provide additional evidence that buying momentum is improving.

BNB Price Forecast: $657 Support and $746 Resistance Define the Next Move

The immediate technical structure places BNB between a nearby support cluster and several layers of overhead resistance.

On the downside, the $684–$692 region represents the first area buyers need to defend. A sustained move below this range could expose the 200-day moving average near $657, which remains an important reference point for the broader market structure.

A decisive daily close below $657 would increase the risk of a deeper correction and weaken the longer-term bullish outlook. It could also bring the bearish projections from the Elliott Wave analyses into greater focus.

Further downside levels include $625 from DamonEdge’s Head and Shoulders analysis, followed by $398–$310 in WhaleFactor’s Elliott Wave projection. MarzellCrypto separately identifies $365 and $290 as potential support areas if the macro breakout retest fails.

On the upside, initial resistance sits around $697–$702, followed by the $710–$722 supply zone. A sustained move through these levels could improve the short-term technical outlook and bring the $746 50-day moving average into focus.

Beyond these immediate barriers, the $813 weekly resistance identified by WhaleFactor remains a significant level. A weekly close above it would invalidate the analyst’s current corrective setup and challenge the bearish Elliott Wave interpretation.

For now, BNB’s technical outlook remains neutral to mildly bearish. The token is holding above its 200-day moving average, but weak momentum and resistance from shorter-term averages suggest that buyers have yet to regain control.

The $690 region therefore remains an important area to watch. A successful defense followed by a recovery above $722 could strengthen the bullish retest scenario. Conversely, a breakdown below $657 would increase the risk of further losses, with $625 emerging as an intermediate downside target before the deeper bearish projections come into consideration.

Ultimately, BNB’s next major move will depend on whether buyers can defend the former breakout structure and restore momentum. Until the price reclaims key resistance levels or breaks its longer-term support, both the bullish recovery and bearish correction scenarios remain open.

title: Suspicious prediction market activity seen before election poll release: NYT
summary: Bets were placed shortly before two recent New York Times/Siena political polls were released to the public, according to a report.
content:
Suspicious prediction market bets were placed shortly before two recent New York Times/Siena political polls were released to the public, according to a report.

Vanderbilt University researchers said a Polymarket user bet almost $200,000 on Oct. 31 that Nebraska Senator Pete Ricketts would be re-elected. An hour later, a Times/Siena poll was released showing Ricketts in the lead.

A Friday New York Times report said while it was not clear if the user had access to inside information, they won more than $77,000.

The user also placed similar large bets on other markets, including Kalshi, the report said.

“There’s a series of circumstances here that it’s hard to write it off as a random occurrence,” said Brett Goldstein of the Vanderbilt Institute of National Security. It “requires further investigation.”

Polymarket said it had spotted the trades and was investigating. Kalshi declined comment.

Cointelegraph reported in April that a US Army soldier had been charged after making more than $400,000 by betting on a prediction market allegedly using nonpublic information tied to a US operation involving then Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

In a statement, the Department of Justice alleged that Master Sergeant Gannon Ken Van Dyke was involved in the planning and execution of Operation Absolute Resolve, which led to the capture of Maduro at a residence in Caracas, Venezuela, in January. 

Van Dyke allegedly used this information to buy “yes” shares in related Polymarket contracts, including “Maduro out by January 31” and “Trump invokes War Powers against Venezuela by January 31,” according to the DOJ.

title: Weekly Review: Prop Firm Match Loses Partners; eToro to Expand in Argentina
summary:
The week brought significant developments across retail
trading, fintech and financial regulation. Prop Firm Match faced a growing
backlash from prop trading firms over its affiliate tracking practices, while
eToro agreed to acquire an Argentine fintech business as it continued expanding
through acq...
content:
The week brought significant developments across retail trading, fintech and financial regulation. Prop Firm Match faced a growing backlash from prop trading firms over its affiliate tracking practices, while eToro agreed to acquire an Argentine fintech business as it continued expanding through acquisitions.

Capital.com also secured a new regulatory licence in Singapore and appointed a former IG executive to lead its local operations.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Regulatory developments included new UK initiatives covering quantum computing and financial crime, alongside changes to transaction reporting requirements. South Africa's regulator also made its withdrawal of Mixirite's licence final.

Meanwhile, artificial intelligence remained a key industry topic, with discussions focusing on how brokers attract customers through AI search and whether investment in the technology can deliver a lasting competitive advantage.

Prop Firm Match Loses Around 21 Partners Over Affiliate Redirect Controversy

Prop Firm Match has lost around 21 prop trading firm partners after acknowledging that clicks on firm profiles and promotional codes opened partner websites through its affiliate links. The exits include Apex Trader Funding, Tradeify, Lucid Trading, Goat Funded Trader, FundingPips and Blue Guardian.

The platform said it disabled the functionality on 29 October and estimated that the potential impact on referral attribution represented a low single-digit percentage of its commissions.

Three years ago, Prop Firm Match launched. Two traders saw a gap in the market for a platform providing simplicity and transparency for prop firm traders. We developed new features not seen before: verified reviews, payout tracking across all payment methods, live spreads, rule overviews, simple ways to compare prop firms, and prop firm expos. Three years in, PFM has had over 25M website visits, reached over 370,000 members, and has given out free challenge accounts worth over $1,400,000 to the PFM community. Over 100 firms apply to be listed each year and go through one of the industry’s most rigorous compliance processes. We also got something wrong. Until yesterday, when someone clicked on a firm or a code on our site, a new tab would open the firm’s site through our affiliate link. This should not have happened. We take full responsibility for it. We have reached out to each of our partners to review this together and reconcile any inaccuracies. We respect any decisions firms have made based on this. We truly appreciate the partners and traders who value the relationship we have built together over the years. We promise you that we will learn from this, hold ourselves to the highest standard, and come back stronger and better.

— Prop Firm Match (@PropFirmMatch) October 31, 2026

However, a source close to the matter said misattributed sales could have appeared as ordinary referrals because tracking cookie periods varied between firms. FundingPips' CEO also said his company had identified the practice in August. The platform has invited current and former partners to review its findings.

eToro Agrees to Acquire Argentine Fintech LB Finanzas

eToro has agreed to acquire Argentine financial app LB Finanzas for an undisclosed amount, marking its fourth acquisition of 2026. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and is intended to establish a stronger local presence in Latin America.

LB Finanzas operates an investment platform offering access to equities, cryptocurrencies and payment services. It is regulated by Argentina's National Securities Commission and Central Bank. The acquisition adds local operations and regulatory infrastructure to eToro's regional expansion plans.

Earlier this year, the company agreed to acquire crypto wallet provider Zengo, completed its purchase of Israeli exchange Bit2C and announced an agreement to acquire US brokerage TradeZero, which is expected to close in 2027.

Capital.com Secures Singapore Licence

Capital.com has received a licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), allowing its local entity to offer securities, collective investment schemes and over-the-counter derivatives, including contracts for differences (CFDs).

The broker plans to begin onboarding clients in early 2027. It has appointed Tony Lim as Chief Executive of its Singapore operations. Lim previously spent nine years at IG Group's Singapore division as CEO and Managing Director. The appointment follows Capital.com's recent regulatory expansion in South Africa and its recruitment of local executives in Brazil and Chile.

The broker has also been exploring licensing opportunities in markets including Japan and Turkey as it expands its international operations.

FCA Invites Financial Firms to Test Quantum Computing

The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has invited financial firms, quantum computing providers and research institutions to test whether quantum technology can improve money laundering and fraud detection.

Participants will join its new Quantum Experimentation Group and work with an artificial dataset developed by the regulator. The trials will compare quantum machine learning approaches with conventional techniques to address financial crime problems identified by the FCA. Registration closes on 31 December, with the programme scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

The initiative follows the regulator's wider preparations for quantum computing, including a separate warning about the need to adopt encryption capable of withstanding future quantum attacks.

South Africa Makes Mixirite Licence Withdrawal Final

South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) has made the withdrawal of Mixirite's financial services licence final, citing material breaches of financial sector laws and failures in client protection.

The decision takes immediate effect after the regulator concluded that the company no longer meets the requirements to operate as a financial services provider. The investigation found that Mixirite's agents used aggressive sales techniques, while unauthorised individuals provided financial advice.

The regulator also identified promises of unrealistic or guaranteed returns, inadequate suitability assessments and governance failures. Mixirite did not oppose the final withdrawal but disputed the findings. Separately, the FSCA expanded its investigation to include four other companies: Complyxpert, Start Stream, Rayn Investments and Advice 365.

Brokers Face New Challenges as AI Chatbots Change Customer Discovery

Artificial intelligence chatbots are changing how retail traders discover and compare brokers, with industry experts warning that strong Google rankings no longer guarantee visibility. Andy Francos, Growth Consultant at Pepperstone, said AI assistants increasingly provide prospective customers with shortlists before they visit individual broker websites.

Wordflow founder Zay Yang highlighted that regulators, comparison platforms and independent media frequently appear ahead of brokers' own websites in AI-generated recommendations. The experts said brokers need accurate, accessible information about licensing, fees and account offerings, preferably presented in plain text rather than scripts or PDFs.

Third-party coverage and credible industry references are also becoming important as AI search engines increasingly determine which brands users consider.

AI Investment Could Raise Costs Without Giving Retail Brokers a Lasting Advantage

Artificial intelligence could help retail brokers improve customer acquisition, automate support and provide more sophisticated trading tools, but the technology may not create a lasting competitive advantage, according to a Finance Magnates analysis by Paul Golden.

Natural language screeners, portfolio analysis and automated execution are among the features changing the trading experience. However, widely available AI models could make these services difficult to differentiate.

Brokers also face integration, monitoring and compliance costs, while increased customer engagement does not necessarily translate into better retention or profitability. The analysis highlights another challenge: as traders increasingly use independent AI agents to compare platforms and execute transactions, brokers could lose control of customer relationships to technology providers.

FCA Revises UK Transaction Reporting Rules

The FCA has finalised changes to the UK's MiFIR transaction reporting framework, aiming to reduce industry costs by more than £100 million annually. The reforms will cut reportable fields from 65 to 52, remove around seven million instruments traded exclusively on EU venues from UK reporting requirements and eliminate duplicate reporting of FX derivatives under MiFIR.

The maximum period for correcting historical reporting errors will also fall from five years to three. The regulator estimates that firms currently spend £493 million annually on transaction reporting. However, implementation will require changes to reporting systems, data management and validation processes.

Quinn Perrott, Co-CEO of TRAction, highlights the operational work firms will need to undertake to adapt to the revised requirements. The new regime will become fully effective on 3 April 2028, although some changes can be adopted earlier.

Finance Magnates Awards 2026 Winners Announced

Finance Magnates has announced the winners of the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, recognising leading companies and CEOs across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services.

The awards honour firms across global, regional and national markets, alongside two CEOs named CEO of the Year 2026 in the B2C and B2B categories.

The week brought significant developments across retail trading, fintech and financial regulation. Prop Firm Match faced a growing backlash from prop trading firms over its affiliate tracking practices, while eToro agreed to acquire an Argentine fintech business as it continued expanding through acquisitions.

Capital.com also secured a new regulatory licence in Singapore and appointed a former IG executive to lead its local operations.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Regulatory developments included new UK initiatives covering quantum computing and financial crime, alongside changes to transaction reporting requirements. South Africa's regulator also made its withdrawal of Mixirite's licence final.

Meanwhile, artificial intelligence remained a key industry topic, with discussions focusing on how brokers attract customers through AI search and whether investment in the technology can deliver a lasting competitive advantage.

Prop Firm Match Loses Around 21 Partners Over Affiliate Redirect Controversy

Prop Firm Match has lost around 21 prop trading firm partners after acknowledging that clicks on firm profiles and promotional codes opened partner websites through its affiliate links. The exits include Apex Trader Funding, Tradeify, Lucid Trading, Goat Funded Trader, FundingPips and Blue Guardian.

The platform said it disabled the functionality on 29 October and estimated that the potential impact on referral attribution represented a low single-digit percentage of its commissions.

Three years ago, Prop Firm Match launched. Two traders saw a gap in the market for a platform providing simplicity and transparency for prop firm traders. We developed new features not seen before: verified reviews, payout tracking across all payment methods, live spreads, rule overviews, simple ways to compare prop firms, and prop firm expos. Three years in, PFM has had over 25M website visits, reached over 370,000 members, and has given out free challenge accounts worth over $1,400,000 to the PFM community. Over 100 firms apply to be listed each year and go through one of the industry’s most rigorous compliance processes. We also got something wrong. Until yesterday, when someone clicked on a firm or a code on our site, a new tab would open the firm’s site through our affiliate link. This should not have happened. We take full responsibility for it. We have reached out to each of our partners to review this together and reconcile any inaccuracies. We respect any decisions firms have made based on this. We truly appreciate the partners and traders who value the relationship we have built together over the years. We promise you that we will learn from this, hold ourselves to the highest standard, and come back stronger and better.

— Prop Firm Match (@PropFirmMatch) October 31, 2026

However, a source close to the matter said misattributed sales could have appeared as ordinary referrals because tracking cookie periods varied between firms. FundingPips' CEO also said his company had identified the practice in August. The platform has invited current and former partners to review its findings.

eToro Agrees to Acquire Argentine Fintech LB Finanzas

eToro has agreed to acquire Argentine financial app LB Finanzas for an undisclosed amount, marking its fourth acquisition of 2026. The transaction remains subject to customary closing conditions and is intended to establish a stronger local presence in Latin America.

LB Finanzas operates an investment platform offering access to equities, cryptocurrencies and payment services. It is regulated by Argentina's National Securities Commission and Central Bank. The acquisition adds local operations and regulatory infrastructure to eToro's regional expansion plans.

Earlier this year, the company agreed to acquire crypto wallet provider Zengo, completed its purchase of Israeli exchange Bit2C and announced an agreement to acquire US brokerage TradeZero, which is expected to close in 2027.

Capital.com Secures Singapore Licence

Capital.com has received a licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), allowing its local entity to offer securities, collective investment schemes and over-the-counter derivatives, including contracts for differences (CFDs).

The broker plans to begin onboarding clients in early 2027. It has appointed Tony Lim as Chief Executive of its Singapore operations. Lim previously spent nine years at IG Group's Singapore division as CEO and Managing Director. The appointment follows Capital.com's recent regulatory expansion in South Africa and its recruitment of local executives in Brazil and Chile.

The broker has also been exploring licensing opportunities in markets including Japan and Turkey as it expands its international operations.

FCA Invites Financial Firms to Test Quantum Computing

The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) has invited financial firms, quantum computing providers and research institutions to test whether quantum technology can improve money laundering and fraud detection.

Participants will join its new Quantum Experimentation Group and work with an artificial dataset developed by the regulator. The trials will compare quantum machine learning approaches with conventional techniques to address financial crime problems identified by the FCA. Registration closes on 31 December, with the programme scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

The initiative follows the regulator's wider preparations for quantum computing, including a separate warning about the need to adopt encryption capable of withstanding future quantum attacks.

South Africa Makes Mixirite Licence Withdrawal Final

South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) has made the withdrawal of Mixirite's financial services licence final, citing material breaches of financial sector laws and failures in client protection.

The decision takes immediate effect after the regulator concluded that the company no longer meets the requirements to operate as a financial services provider. The investigation found that Mixirite's agents used aggressive sales techniques, while unauthorised individuals provided financial advice.

The regulator also identified promises of unrealistic or guaranteed returns, inadequate suitability assessments and governance failures. Mixirite did not oppose the final withdrawal but disputed the findings. Separately, the FSCA expanded its investigation to include four other companies: Complyxpert, Start Stream, Rayn Investments and Advice 365.

Brokers Face New Challenges as AI Chatbots Change Customer Discovery

Artificial intelligence chatbots are changing how retail traders discover and compare brokers, with industry experts warning that strong Google rankings no longer guarantee visibility. Andy Francos, Growth Consultant at Pepperstone, said AI assistants increasingly provide prospective customers with shortlists before they visit individual broker websites.

Wordflow founder Zay Yang highlighted that regulators, comparison platforms and independent media frequently appear ahead of brokers' own websites in AI-generated recommendations. The experts said brokers need accurate, accessible information about licensing, fees and account offerings, preferably presented in plain text rather than scripts or PDFs.

Third-party coverage and credible industry references are also becoming important as AI search engines increasingly determine which brands users consider.

AI Investment Could Raise Costs Without Giving Retail Brokers a Lasting Advantage

Artificial intelligence could help retail brokers improve customer acquisition, automate support and provide more sophisticated trading tools, but the technology may not create a lasting competitive advantage, according to a Finance Magnates analysis by Paul Golden.

Natural language screeners, portfolio analysis and automated execution are among the features changing the trading experience. However, widely available AI models could make these services difficult to differentiate.

Brokers also face integration, monitoring and compliance costs, while increased customer engagement does not necessarily translate into better retention or profitability. The analysis highlights another challenge: as traders increasingly use independent AI agents to compare platforms and execute transactions, brokers could lose control of customer relationships to technology providers.

FCA Revises UK Transaction Reporting Rules

The FCA has finalised changes to the UK's MiFIR transaction reporting framework, aiming to reduce industry costs by more than £100 million annually. The reforms will cut reportable fields from 65 to 52, remove around seven million instruments traded exclusively on EU venues from UK reporting requirements and eliminate duplicate reporting of FX derivatives under MiFIR.

The maximum period for correcting historical reporting errors will also fall from five years to three. The regulator estimates that firms currently spend £493 million annually on transaction reporting. However, implementation will require changes to reporting systems, data management and validation processes.

Quinn Perrott, Co-CEO of TRAction, highlights the operational work firms will need to undertake to adapt to the revised requirements. The new regime will become fully effective on 3 April 2028, although some changes can be adopted earlier.

content:
2026-11-06T23:54:00.000+02:00

Friday, 06/11/2026 | 21:54 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Dollar stablecoins can serve Nigerian retail users only through a locally incorporated, CBN-licensed issuer.
  • Stablecoin payments or remittances might require separate CBN approval.

Nigeria has adopted regulations for non-security virtual assets that make it one of the most restrictive stablecoin market-access regimes currently in force.

According to the document, published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), foreign issuers must build a locally licensed operation before making their tokens available to retail customers. New rules combine local incorporation, token-level approval, capital requirements and separate permissions for payment functions.

The regulations, effective from 5 November, apply to overseas companies targeting Nigerian users even when those businesses have no physical presence in the country.

Dollar Stablecoins Need a Nigerian Issuer

The CBN divides stablecoins into two categories. Class 1 covers tokens pegged to the naira, while Class 2 applies to those referencing foreign currencies, such as dollar-backed tokens USDT or USDC.

Foreign issuers are effectively cut off from the local retail customers until they establish a Nigerian company, obtain Class 2 issuer licence, and CBN approval for their tokens

That local company must maintain at least NGN15 billion (approximately $11.1 million) in paid-up capital and provide operational liquidity for redemptions in Nigeria.

Tokens must be fully backed by assets denominated in their reference currency, with an additional 2% buffer. The issuer must also appoint a Nigerian bank to process local redemption requests.

Stablecoin Payments Require a Second Approval

The new framework divides oversight: the SEC remains responsible for trading and investment-related custody, while the CBN controls payment and money-transfer services.

An SEC-licensed crypto platform can therefore list a stablecoin or hold it for trading clients. However, for customer transfers, merchant payments, remittances, payment gateways or stored-value products separate CBN authorisation is required.

These permissions are activity-specific. A company authorised for custody or exchange cannot assume that the same approval covers a P2P service or cross-border payments.

Providers of these non-issuance services must also maintain at least NGN1 billion, or approximately $741,000, in additional capital. Moreover, a SEC-regulated platform cannot use the same funds to satisfy both regulators’ requirements.

Conversions between naira and a foreign-currency stablecoin may require an authorised foreign-exchange channel, transaction reporting and specific CBN approval.

This regulatory approach creates a layered model in which the token, its issuer and each payment function must all receive the appropriate permission.

Nigeria Is Already One of Africa’s Largest Crypto Markets

The rules apply to a market where cryptoassets are used for more than speculative trading. Stablecoins provide Nigerian citizens and businesses with access to dollar-denominated value and an alternative channel for cross-border payments when conventional transfers are expensive or foreign currency is difficult to obtain.

Chainalysis estimated that Nigeria recorded $38.1 billion in crypto activity between July 2025 and June 2026, slightly below South Africa’s $39.3 billion. Nigeria also ranked third in the company’s global grassroots adoption index, which measures patterns of everyday use rather than absolute transaction volume.

Stablecoin activity through peer-to-peer channels increased more than sixfold between 2022 and 2026, from $2.3 billion to $14.6 billion, according to the same study. This combination of dollar demand, cross-border use and growing domestic distribution helps explain the structure of the CBN regime.

The regulator is permitting stablecoins, but wants their issuance, conversion and payment functions to pass through locally supervised companies and approved financial channels.

Existing operators have 180 days to apply, but may continue only at their current scale during the transition. They must register within 30 days and begin supervisory reporting within 60 days, making expansion dependent on securing the new approvals.

title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
FinCEN issued a final order under section 9714(a) that will bar U.S. financial institutions from sending or receiving funds with MEXC Global 30 days after Federal Register publication, ...
content:
The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said.

FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC.

Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking.

Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says.

What the order does — and when

The order, signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations.

Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending.

Background on MEXC

Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions.

Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned the same month that the platform was marketing to local investors without a licence. Seychelles’ Financial Services Authority said in May 2026 it took action against MX Global Ltd for unlicensed virtual-asset operations — footnoted in FinCEN’s order.

Those compliance gaps matter because the illicit-flow thesis is specific, not guilt by association. Beyond Russia, FinCEN cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers, nearly $26 million with the OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions-evasion network, and almost $200 million tied to the A7A5 stablecoin. DPRK facilitators and cybercrime flows are also alleged. MEXC has not issued a public response to the Friday order; its main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon.

Why it matters for bitcoin markets

Practically, once the order bites, U.S. banks, money transmitters and other covered firms cannot move dollars or crypto to MEXC wallets or accounts. Offshore users may keep trading peer-to-peer, but dollar on-ramps and any bank that still clears for MEXC become legal risk. The template tracks earlier 9714 cut-offs of venues such as Bitzlato, and it lands beside a busy sanctions week that has already seen North Korea crypto designations, an Iranian exchange action, and Russia’s push to put bitcoin trading on the Moscow Exchange.

Whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or quietly reroutes liquidity is the open question. For now the paper trail is clear: a final FinCEN order under 9714(a), a 30-day fuse after Federal Register publication, and Treasury’s claim of at least $16 billion in illicit volume sitting behind the cut-off.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Finance Magnates Awards 2026 Winners Announced
summary: Finance Magnates has announced the winners of the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, recognising leading companies and CEOs across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services. The awards honour firms across global, regional and national markets, alongside two CEOs named CEO of the Year 2026 ...
content:
Finance Magnates has announced the winners of the Finance Magnates Awards 2026, recognising leading companies and CEOs across online trading, fintech, payments and financial services. The awards honour firms across global, regional and national markets, alongside two CEOs named CEO of the Year 2026 in the B2C and B2B categories.

The winners were announced at the Finance Magnates Awards Gala Dinner & Ceremony in Limassol, Cyprus on November 6, 2026, bringing together companies and professionals from across the financial industry for an evening of recognition.

The Finance Magnates Awards recognise firms across a wide range of categories, including brokerage services, proprietary trading, institutional trading, payments, financial technology and services for brokers.

The 2026 awards feature winners across Global, Regional and National categories for Brokerage (B2C), alongside dedicated awards for Fintech (B2B) firms operating in Institutional Trading, Services for Brokers and Tech for Brokers.

Finance Magnates Awards 2026: Brokerage (B2C) Winners

The Brokerage (B2C) awards recognise companies serving traders and investors across global markets. The winners span brokerage firms and proprietary trading businesses, with awards covering areas such as innovation, customer service, trading conditions and overall performance.

Global Award Winners

The Global categories recognise companies operating across international markets.

  • Most Established Broker 2026: Tickmill

  • Best Rising Star Broker 2026: IQ Broker

  • Most Innovative Broker 2026: FXT

  • Most Trusted Broker 2026: TradingPRO
