title: Paraguay Bank Crisis Sends USDT to 13% Premium After Ueno Freeze Hits 3M Customers
summary:
Key Takeaways: Bybit P2P listing also went about 13% cheaper than Paraguay’s official dollar rate in USDT. The failure of Ueno Bank was a limitation of access for about 3
The post Paraguay Bank Crisis Sends USDT to 13% Premium After Ueno Freeze Hits 3M Customers appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Bybit P2P listing also went about 13% cheaper than Paraguay’s official dollar rate in USDT.
  • The failure of Ueno Bank was a limitation of access for about 3 million people.
  • Stablecoins are being used by local residents as a payment method, source of liquidity, and as a dollar exposure.

Paraguay’s banking crisis has seeped into the crypto world as demand for dollar-stablecoins surged following the Ueno Bank digital lending platform’s failure, which took millions of customer accounts offline.

One USDT listing on Bybit’s Paraguay peer-to-peer market asked for 6,942 guaraníes per token, around 13% above the central bank’s Nov. 4 reference rate of 6,144.02 guaraníes per US dollar. The figure is a quoted P2P offer and other quotes were materially different.

  • Ueno Freeze Pushes Users Toward Crypto Liquidity
  • USDT and USDC Gain Local Demand
    • Deposit Payouts Begin While Stablecoins Fill the Gap

Ueno Freeze Pushes Users Toward Crypto Liquidity

The bank, Ueno, had emerged as a big Paraguayan digital bank, with some 3 million users out of a nation of some 6.5 million people. It is also keeping about $850 million of public money, reports Reuters.

The Central Bank of Paraguay began its resolution process because Ueno’s solvency level was below the minimum threshold of 50%. The process was intended to safeguard depositors and stability of the financial system, the regulator said.

Since there has been no access to banks, some have been turning to crypto assets as a quick way to fund themselves.

Read More: Jupiter Lend Halts Withdrawals Amid $6.3B Binance Hack Fears Despite Zero Exposure

USDT and USDC Gain Local Demand

USDT and USDC prices in guaraní had climbed some 8% over the past weeks. But he said the boost was not all because of the Ueno crisis. The process started in October, and also indicated the weakening of the US dollar’s value in relation to the guaraní.

This bit of distinction is important as a local stablecoin premium might signify a number of things: banking restrictions, non-dollar payment methods available, banking dollar demand, P2P conditions and liquidity.

However, the Ueno shutdown opened a window of opportunity for crypto holders who would like to access their funds during the period of the traditional deposit delay.

Deposit Payouts Begin While Stablecoins Fill the Gap

Paraguay’s central bank has started payment of deposits from Nov. 5. Those in the first group are eligible depositors whose balance is up to 10 million guaranieres, who have no outstanding loans with Ueno and their account at other financial institutions is active. The protection of deposits in the country comes up to 228.3 million guaraníes per depositor and per institution.

The banking crisis also brought forth a political crisis. Illegalities surrounding Ueno brought about the resignation of President Santiago Peña on Nov. 5 when lawmakers turned to impeachment. Peña denied wrongdoing.

Mensaje del Presidente de la República, Santiago Peña, al pueblo paraguayo. https://t.co/RBz6IfFV9L

— Santiago Peña (@SantiPenap) November 5, 2026

The key indicator for cryptos is the rush for dollar liquidity. In his account of the developments, Tether’s CEO Paolo Ardoino said USDT is a financial lifeline for hundreds of millions of people around the world, while Paraguay is a new example of how stablecoins can become more valuable if access to traditional banking suddenly becomes more challenging.

title: Thailand to Block Bitget on Dec. 5 After SEC Files Criminal Complaint Over Licensing
summary:
Key Takeaways: Due to the frequent violations of privacy by hackers, Thailand will ban Bitget from Dec. 5. The SEC initiated action against Bitget operator BG Limited for securities and
The post Thailand to Block Bitget on Dec. 5 After SEC Files Criminal Complaint Over Licensing appeared first on Cr...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Due to the frequent violations of privacy by hackers, Thailand will ban Bitget from Dec. 5.
  • The SEC initiated action against Bitget operator BG Limited for securities and commodity fraud charges.
  • Users were advised to check their assets on the platform prior to the cut-off date.

Thailand is aiming to sever local access to cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, citing violations from the country’s securities regulator on running an unlicensed digital asset business.

The Securities and Exchange Commission yesterday announced Bitget’s website, its domains, and its application will be inaccessible in Thailand starting Dec. 5, 2026, providing users with about a month to prepare.

  • Bitget Faces Criminal Complaint Over Thai Crypto Services
  • Users Face a Dec. 5 Access Deadline
    • Bitget Was Already Seeking a Licensed Route Into Thailand

Bitget Faces Criminal Complaint Over Thai Crypto Services

The Thailand Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has lodged a criminal complaint against the company behind Bitget.com, BG Limited. The regulator found that between 2022 and 2025, Bitget provided digital asset trading service to users in Thailand, took trading fees, and had a website in Thai language that quoted crypto prices in Thai baht.

The SEC also highlighted that Thai-language marketing was done on social media platforms such as X, Telegram, and TikTok. Such activities constitute the operation of a digital asset exchange business without the necessary license under the Digital Asset Business Emergency Decree, the regulator added.

Kritsana Kritsananuwat, the SEC alleges, helped promote Bitget through Facebook and YouTube, a second complaint against the individual. The case is being investigated by Thailand’s economic crime groups.

Read More: 25 BLOOM Participants Join 3 Asian Central Banks to Advance Cross-Border Digital Money

Users Face a Dec. 5 Access Deadline

The SEC has already sent information covering Bitget’s website, associated domains and mobile app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society. After its block, users from Thailand might no longer have access to the platform by regular local internet connections.

In particular, the regulator told the investors to act on their assets on Bitget before the deadline of Dec. 5 to mitigate possible disruption. This warning has nothing to do with the assets being lost or frozen by customers, the SEC said. The contention regards Bitget’s regulatory standing and how consumers can access this platform locally.

Bitget Was Already Seeking a Licensed Route Into Thailand

The action follows Bitget’s reports on the proposed acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a local crypto exchange and brokerage.

On Oct. 20, Bitget revealed its plans for the offer by acquiring an interest in BTGT Management (Thailand). This transaction is subject to regulatory approval and is subject to other closing factors.

That creates a notable regulatory split. As Bitget tries to open up a branch office in Thailand, its SEC says that one of Bitget’s previous platforms previously operated without a licence for Thai users.

The planned purchase does not automatically cure un вет bitget.com via the past or even current functions within the nation: a SEC criminal complaint will continue via investigators, prosecutors and also courts.

The challenge for crypto users from Thailand is a bit easier: Dec. 5 is the day to watch at Bitget.

title: Conflux – Web3’s Next Billion Users
summary: David Wei Liang is a vice president at Conflux Network, the Layer-1 blockchain built around its Tree-Graph consensus and positioned as a bridge between China’s engineering ecosystem and global Web3 markets. His career has centred on distributed systems. He earned a PhD in computer science at the Chi...
content:
Skip to content

David Wei Liang is a vice president at Conflux Network, the Layer-1 blockchain built around its Tree-Graph consensus and positioned as a bridge between China’s engineering ecosystem and global Web3 markets. His career has centred on distributed systems. He earned a PhD in computer science at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, studying peer-to-peer networks, followed by postdoctoral research in distributed systems. He then worked at Huawei’s Noah’s Ark Lab in Hong Kong and became chief blockchain expert at China Telecom, where he led work on the blockchain-enabled SIM card, BSIM.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Most of crypto, Liang argues, competes for the same users and capital, moving them between chains with bridges, compatible tooling and higher yields. The larger opportunity sits outside that circle: close to six billion mobile subscribers, five billion internet users and billions of banking customers, plus a projected wave of AI agents that Huawei estimates could reach 900 billion by 2035. His view is that moving existing users only changes market share, while creating new demand changes the size of the market. Telecom operators, with decades of relationships with billions of subscribers and the physical networks every digital economy runs on, are in his view the most natural route in.

The practical case rests on BSIM, which turns the SIM card already in everyone’s phone into a secure wallet that generates and stores private keys and signs transactions without the keys ever leaving the card. Liang describes a pilot in Shanghai, a commercial deployment in Hong Kong through a licensed telecom operator combining roaming data and stablecoin payments, and an enterprise rollout with an insurance partner in Hunan. His main lesson is that people should not have to become crypto experts to use Web3, and that asking newcomers to write down a 12-word recovery phrase works against mass adoption. He sees digital identity as the most valuable starting point, linking a subscriber’s network identity to a wallet with consent, so that a phone number can work as a payment address and operators could reward users for everyday calls.

The conversation then moves to AI. Liang argues that agents need money software can spend in very small amounts and settle instantly, with spending limits enforced in code, and points to standards such as x402 that already make this possible. His rule for what belongs on-chain is simple: anything that needs speed stays off-chain, while anything that needs agreement, such as payments, commitments and settlement, goes on the ledger. On privacy, he argues that personal AI agents will learn far more about their users than Web2 platforms ever did, and that combining telecom identity, wallets and blockchain could let people authorize agents without handing their data to a few large companies. He closes with stablecoins including USDT0 and AxCNH now on Conflux, a network upgrade completed in October, and his test for success: Web3 wins when it disappears into everyday life, the way nobody says they are using TCP/IP.

title: Moonshot AI Eyes 8,000+ Nvidia Blackwell GPUs Through European Cloud Providers Despite US Chip Curbs
summary: Moonshot AI is exploring access to more than 8,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in Europe as China’s AI developers seek computing power beyond domestic supply.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVIDIA

Moonshot AI is exploring access to more than 8,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs in Europe as China’s AI developers seek computing power beyond domestic supply.

CNBC reported on November 5 that the Beijing-based Kimi developer has discussed renting advanced GPU capacity from European cloud operators, although no agreement has been confirmed.

Moonshot AI Seeks More Nvidia Blackwell GPU Capacity

Moonshot AI has reportedly approached European neocloud providers about renting large clusters of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs to expand its computing resources. The discussions involve access to more than 8,000 processors, potentially supporting both AI inference and model training.

Moonshot AI is leasing Nvidia Blackwell GPU clusters from European data centers and cloud providers to secure advanced computing power amid US chip restrictions. Source: CNBC via X

According to CNBC, three people familiar with the discussions said the Chinese AI company has been actively pursuing additional computing capacity in Europe. One source described Moonshot’s efforts as “very aggressive” as it seeks access to Nvidia’s advanced hardware.

The proposed arrangements would allow Moonshot to use computing infrastructure physically located outside China without bringing the restricted processors into the country. Under this model, European data center operators would maintain the hardware while Moonshot would pay for remote access to its computing capacity.

The financial terms could also reflect the regulatory complications surrounding such arrangements. One source told CNBC that a proposal had called for Moonshot to pay an upfront premium of 30% to 50% above the amount charged to a non-Chinese customer. However, the discussions remain preliminary, and there is no confirmation that the company has accepted those terms or secured the capacity.

European Cloud Rentals Raise Questions About US Chip Restrictions

The discussions highlight a gap between restrictions on physical semiconductor shipments and the growing international market for cloud-based AI computing.

Washington has restricted direct exports of Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell processors to Chinese customers over national security concerns. The controls are intended to limit China’s access to high-performance computing hardware that can support advanced AI development.

Nvidia requires data center partners to reserve at least 51% of future services for non-Chinese customers to restrict remote GPU access by Chinese firms. Source: @MartiniGuyYT via X

However, renting computing capacity from an independent overseas operator presents a different regulatory question from purchasing restricted chips and transporting them into China. The customer can execute AI workloads remotely while the GPUs remain inside a data center in another country.

This distinction has become a growing concern for US policymakers. A Congressional Research Service report published in April 2026 identified remote access to advanced AI computing through cloud services as a potential weakness in existing export-control enforcement. It noted that foreign AI developers could access advanced processors through cloud providers even when direct hardware shipments were restricted.

Washington has since taken steps to clarify the rules governing overseas chip shipments. On May 31, the US Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security clarified that export license requirements also apply to advanced computing chips shipped to companies headquartered in China, even when their receiving entities operate outside the country.

A Reuters report noted that the updated guidance did not require data centers to stop using the chips or discontinue servicing existing equipment. This distinction is important because restrictions on physical exports do not automatically resolve questions surrounding remote access to independently operated computing infrastructure.

The European rental discussions therefore expose an unresolved regulatory challenge. While Washington can restrict the movement and transfer of advanced processors, controlling access to computing services hosted by independent operators in other jurisdictions presents a different enforcement task.

Previous Thailand Access Allegations Put Moonshot Under Scrutiny

Moonshot’s reported European expansion follows an earlier controversy involving Nvidia’s Blackwell hardware in Southeast Asia.

In July 2026, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios accused the Chinese AI developer of obtaining access to restricted Nvidia processors through facilities in Thailand. The allegation emerged following the release of Moonshot’s Kimi K3 model, which attracted attention for its performance against advanced US AI systems.

U.S. export controls restrict direct Blackwell chip shipments to China but permit overseas cloud rentals, despite previous White House allegations that Moonshot used a Thailand-based data center. Source: @wallstengine via X

Kratsios said the company had “acquired GB300-equipped servers and has accessed GB300s in Thailand, likely to train its AI models.”

The GB300 is part of Nvidia’s Blackwell generation. The White House’s remarks raised questions about how Chinese AI developers could obtain access to advanced American processors through overseas infrastructure despite Washington’s export restrictions.

The allegation also increased attention on the role of third-party data center operators and international computing providers in the AI hardware supply chain.

Moonshot did not publicly confirm the reported Thailand arrangement in response to the earlier allegations. The latest European discussions indicate that access to overseas computing infrastructure remains an important part of the company’s reported capacity expansion efforts.

Kimi’s Growing Demand Increases Computing Requirements

Moonshot’s interest in additional Nvidia hardware comes as the company expands its AI model development and commercial services.

The startup launched Kimi K3 in July 2026, describing it as a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model designed for advanced reasoning, coding, and knowledge-intensive tasks. Moonshot said the model delivered performance approaching Anthropic’s Fable system, placing its latest release in direct competition with advanced models developed by US technology companies.

The launch also exposed pressure on the company’s existing computing infrastructure. Following a surge in demand, Moonshot temporarily paused new subscriptions to Kimi K3 to prioritize computing resources for existing users.

In a July announcement, the company acknowledged the capacity challenge, stating: “We’re adding capacity as fast as we can and will reopen new subscription spots in batches.”

The situation illustrates why additional inference capacity could be particularly important. Training requires substantial computing resources to develop and improve models, while inference relies on GPUs to process user requests and generate responses after deployment. Growing adoption can therefore increase infrastructure requirements even after a model has completed its initial training.

Moonshot has also been linked to other Nvidia computing arrangements. A July 2026 report by Bloomberg, cited by Reuters, said the company had access to approximately 20,000 Nvidia chips through an agreement with Alibaba. Those processors were reported to belong to Nvidia’s older Hopper generation, although Alibaba disputed claims that it had supplied H200 chips.

The reported discussions with European neocloud operators represent a separate potential source of access to newer Blackwell infrastructure. They could help Moonshot expand its computing resources for both model development and serving users, although the scale of any eventual arrangement remains unknown.

For Nvidia, the reported interest highlights continued demand for its advanced processors across international AI markets, including from developers facing restrictions on direct access to the hardware.

Whether Moonshot secures the proposed European capacity will depend on commercial negotiations, infrastructure availability and the regulatory requirements governing remote access. For now, the discussions offer another indication that competition for advanced AI computing is extending beyond traditional hardware purchases into a global market for rented GPU capacity.

title: Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Signing System
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance claimed that their $6.34 billion hack happened over a month-long attack campaign. Hackers’ applications included fake job interviews, malware and using compromised internal AI tooling. Around $2.85
The post Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Si...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance claimed that their $6.34 billion hack happened over a month-long attack campaign.
  • Hackers’ applications included fake job interviews, malware and using compromised internal AI tooling.
  • Around $2.85 billion in funds has been frozen, with 98% of affected tokens being topped up.

Binance has released its first detailed account of the October 29th breach, revealing that attackers spent months building access before reaching the exchange’s wallet-signing infrastructure.

https://t.co/sU9dUqLQDH

— Binance (@binance) November 3, 2026

Social engineering, endpoint compromise and the misuse of the Ethereum transaction authorization capabilities were all cited by the crypto exchange as causatives in the incident.

Read More: Binance $6.3B Hack Triggers FBI Probe While $3B in Stolen Crypto Gets Frozen

  • Binance Hack Started Months Before the $6.34B Theft
  • Internal AI Tool Became Part of the Attack Path
    • Attackers Exploited EIP-7702 to Keep Moving Crypto
    • Binance Freezes $2.85B and Replenishes 98% of Tokens

Binance Hack Started Months Before the $6.34B Theft

Binance says the hack started back in June, when a newly hired Wallet DevOps engineer downloaded a modified software package during the installation of an AI coding tool.

Binance noticed that incident and rotated credentials and replaced the device. But the attacker had already learned information about how the engineer worked on wallet infrastructure and its other team members. Walls was targeted again in September using a legitimate job-search website.

The attacker pretended to be a recruiter, followed by a video interview, and then requested the engineer’s attention to download a coding assignment. Malware in the repository was used to run during installation and write to the employee’s work computer.

Read More: Binance Restores 15 Networks After $6.3B Hack While Outflows Surge to $5.8B

Internal AI Tool Became Part of the Attack Path

The attackers were then able to use the impersonated device and AI tool to gain access into the systems of two other engineers, Binance said.

By October 20th, they found a token for container deployments in a Wallet DevOps employee’s possession. A stolen set of credentials was leveraged to launch a container and send malicious code into Binance’s wallet environment on October 29th.

The hackers subsequently accessed an internal wallet-signing service, thus circumventing the exchange’s typical withdrawal procedure.

Attackers Exploited EIP-7702 to Keep Moving Crypto

Several networks were vulnerable to the hack. The attacker has received 5 Binance hot wallets with a total of 233.46 million XRP. Other wallets made another 970,503 SOL and 44.2 million OP transfers, followed by 18,270 BTC transfers.

EIP-7702 is a feature in Ethereum that enables delegation of execution rights from an account to a smart contract, which the attackers exploited.

According to Binance, their research was able to detect a malicious nonce manipulation using 50 signing transactions. They were never removed after the withdrawals were paused and withdrawing was not an option to stop all transfers instantly.

Also, the Multi-Party Computation wallet setup made it more difficult since there was no single private key to take out the malicious authorizations at a speedy go.

Binance Freezes $2.85B and Replenishes 98% of Tokens

Around $6.34 billion in digital assets were affected, according to Binance co-CEO Richard Teng. According to the CEO, more than $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted with assistance from the law enforcement and the tokens’ issuers and blockchain intelligence companies.

On 29 October, Binance was the target of one of the most sophisticated attacks the digital asset industry has ever seen. ~$6.34B in assets were impacted. We take full responsibility and we’re making it right.

No user bears the loss. We set aside more than the full amount required. At this moment, 98% of impacted tokens had been replenished; we’re completing the remaining 2%. Withdrawals have broadly resumed.

This wasn’t one mistake or one breach – it was a months-long campaign. We’re publishing the full report because the lessons go far beyond Binance.

~$2.85B has already been frozen or intercepted with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain intelligence firms. The speed of coordination could not be matched in traditional finance.

— Richard Teng (@_RichardTeng) November 3, 2026

Binance has pledged to take the hit, not the buyers. By October 31st, token assets representing 98% had been renewed, and the remainder of less liquid assets were being bought in.

The exchange has since rebuilt wallet systems and internal AI tools impacted, replaced compromised devices, revoked credentials and added AI-based behavioural anomaly detection.

title: Signal Week (formerly Paris Blockchain Week) Returns to Paris in July 2027
summary: Paris, France, 5th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Paris, France, 5th November 2026, Chainwire

Paris, France, November 5th, 2026, Chainwire

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, opens 2027 Edition as Paris Becomes the Capital of Finance, AI and Robotics.

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, has opened its 2027 edition, which will take place on July 6–7, 2027, at the Palais des Congrès de Paris, in the same week as RAISE Summit, the world’s leading AI event, and MACHINA Summit, Europe’s leading Physical AI event.

The announcement follows a successful seventh edition in April 2026, which marked a new chapter for the event. In 2026, Paris Blockchain Week officially became Signal Week, the Institutional Summit for Digital Assets, reflecting an audience that has shifted decisively towards banks, asset managers, regulators and governments.

For one week in July, the events will bring digital assets, artificial intelligence and robotics into the same city at the same time, gathering the people building the next generation of financial infrastructure and the technologies that will run on it.

A more institutional room

Signal Week 2027 will bring together banks, financial institutions, digital asset companies, technology firms, investors, policymakers and government representatives, with major institutions such as BlackRock, J.P. Morgan, Citi, Fidelity and BNP Paribas confirming participation.

The 2027 edition is designed around the institutions now shaping digital assets, with BlackRock, J.P. Morgan, Citi, Fidelity and BNP Paribas already confirmed. Its programme will span banks and financial institutions, fintech and payments, AI and agentic finance, and the policymakers and public officials setting the rules for the sector.

The 2026 edition saw unprecedented government participation, with more than 400 attendees from the public sector. They included Laurent Nuñez, Minister of the Interior of France; Anne Le Hénanff, Minister-Delegate for AI and Digital Affairs; and Jean-Didier Berger, Deputy of the French National Assembly. Across the event, Signal Week welcomed more than 10,000 attendees from over 100 countries, with 70% at C-suite level.

In a conversation with theCUBE and NYSE Wired, Michael Amar, Co-founder of Signal Week, said, “We really want to be the place where we bridge traditional finance and digital assets. In 2019, people were making fun of us, but actually it’s where the market is, finally.”

Charlie Méraud, Co-founder of Signal Week, added, “Signal Week is where institutional finance does business in digital assets. When we launched in 2019, we had to explain blockchain and crypto. This industry needed a room for these players to connect and start actually doing business. Signal Week is this room.”

Watch the full interview here.

Curated meetings

Signal Week 2027 will also offer curated one-to-one meetings, helping attendees connect with the right people and get the most out of the event. The 2026 edition facilitated more than 53,000 meetings, resulting in a rewarding networking experience for all attendees.

The VIP Dinner at Château de Versailles

On the eve of the summit, Signal Week will host its VIP Dinner at the Château de Versailles. The 2026 dinner brought together 500+ leaders from finance, technology and government, representing $37 trillion in assets. The 2027 edition will again convene senior figures from traditional finance, digital assets and public policy.

Super Early Bird tickets now live

Super Early Bird tickets for Signal Week 2027 are available from today at the lowest price the event will be offered at, until November 25th. Tickets are available at signalweek.com/tickets.

About Signal Week

Signal Week, formerly Paris Blockchain Week, is the Institutional Summit for Digital Assets, bringing together the financial institutions, digital asset companies, investors, policymakers and technology leaders shaping on-chain finance. Since 2019, its community has grown to more than 10,000 attendees from over 100 countries, with 70% at the C-suite level.

title: Circle’s $182M ARC Token Sale Drives Q3 Growth While USDC Onchain Volume Hits $13.9T
summary:
Key Takeaways: Circle raised an additional $182 million in the ARC token presale during Q3. Onchain transaction volume rose almost 50% YoY for USDC to $13.9 trillion. Reserve income dropped
The post Circle’s $182M ARC Token Sale Drives Q3 Growth While USDC Onchain Volume Hits $13.9T appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Circle raised an additional $182 million in the ARC token presale during Q3.
  • Onchain transaction volume rose almost 50% YoY for USDC to $13.9 trillion.
  • Reserve income dropped by 8% and USDC share closed the quarter at 27%.

The results of Circle in the third quarter indicate that the business is becoming less reliant on reserve income. The stablecoin issuer reported being confident with the top line and the bottom line as the ARC token presale boosted revenues and USDC further onchained.

  • ARC Token Adds $182M to Circle’s Revenue Mix
  • Arc Expands Beyond Circle’s Stablecoin Business
    • USDC Volume Jumps to $13.9T
    • Reserve Income Slips Despite Higher USDC Circulation

ARC Token Adds $182M to Circle’s Revenue Mix

Circle reports total revenue and a reserve income of $865 million in Q3 2026, compared to 17% growth a year ago. Much of that increase was attributable to other revenues, which rose an impressive 627% to $207 million. One of the figures allocated to the ARC token presale is $182 million.

Net income from continuing operations increased five percent from the prior-year level to $226 million; adjusted EBITDA grew by 85 percent on the year to $317 million. Diluted earnings per share were up to $0.84 from $0.64 a year ago.

Read More: Circle Brings USDC and EURC Into SAP Workflows Powering 84% of Global Commerce

Arc Expands Beyond Circle’s Stablecoin Business

Arc launched on public mainnet on Sept. 16 with more than 100 institutional and ecosystem builders. Circle also released the initial 10 billion tokens of ARC. Security, usefulness and governance are the main features of the token as Arc moves towards a proof-of-stake format in 2027.

The token sale provides Circle with additional income streams involving USDC’s reserves’ traditional economics.

USDC Volume Jumps to $13.9T

Despite the weakened economic conditions of the reserve business, the activity of USDC continued to be fairly good. Average circulation for USDC during the quarter was $73.3 billion, increasing 8% over a year ago. The volume of transactions increased by 49%, reaching $13.9 trillion onchain.

At the end of the quarter, USDC had $73.9 billion worth of currency in circulation. Similarly, onchain wallet addresses with more than $10 in USDC on their wallet increased 16% in a year to 7.3 million, Circle reported.

The company, however, lost 183 bps from a year ago to 27% of the market in fiat-based stablecoins.

Read More: Circle Targets 100+ Markets and $25B Flows in Major USDC Payments Expansion Deal

Reserve Income Slips Despite Higher USDC Circulation

Circle’s reserves decreased $8 million to $658M. The largest pressure was from the reserve return rate, which fell 61 basis points to 3.5%. That was tempered a bit by a rise in circulation of the USDC.

The effect of distribution, transaction and other costs decreased by 8% to $412 million, which helped Revenue less Distribution costs total $453 million.

Circle adopted a multi-years target to increase the circulation of USDC at a compound annual rate of 40% through market cycles. It also impacted other revenues in 2026 with a guidance of $310 million to $330 million, which encompasses amounts from recognized ARC token presale revenue.

title: ApeChain Shifts APE and USDC to Chainlink CCIP Across Yuga Labs’ Cross-Chain Ecosystem
summary:
Key Takeaways: ApeChain is transitioning its cross-chain technical infrastructure from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP. APE, USDC and other significant assets will be transferred to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard. The
The post ApeChain Shifts APE and USDC to Chainlink CCIP Across Yuga Labs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • ApeChain is transitioning its cross-chain technical infrastructure from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP.
  • APE, USDC and other significant assets will be transferred to Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Token (CCT) standard.
  • The upgrade will be rolled out for the wider Yuga Labs ecosystem such as Bored Ape Yacht Club use cases.

ApeChain is revamping its cross-chain capabilities to adopt Chainlink CCIP as the universal standard for cross-chain transfers. The update includes all major tokens on APEChain such as APE, USDC and will be used to establish an identical interoperable layer throughout the Yuga Labs ecosystem.

NEW: ApeChain is deprecating its legacy cross-chain solution & migrating to Chainlink CCIP.

CCIP is now becoming the canonical cross-chain infra across the entire Yuga Labs ecosystem, starting with its flagship @BoredApeYC use cases, ApeChain, & the APE token.

Two communities. One ecosystem. One secure cross-chain standard.

— Chainlink (@chainlink) November 4, 2026

  • ApeChain Makes Chainlink CCIP Its Cross-Chain Standard
  • APE and USDC Will Become Cross-Chain Tokens
    • CCIP Gives ApeChain One Integration Layer
    • Yuga Labs Unifies Cross-Chain Infrastructure

ApeChain Makes Chainlink CCIP Its Cross-Chain Standard

ApeChain said it will migrate away from LayerZero and adopt Chainlink’s Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, as its canonical cross-chain stack. Chainlink said the rollout will extend beyond ApeChain itself, covering flagship Bored Ape Yacht Club applications and the APE token.

ApeChain is working with @chainlink to strengthen our infrastructure for the future.

We will be migrating from LayerZero to Chainlink CCIP as our canonical cross-chain stack across the @yugalabs ecosystem, including @BoredApeYC.

With CCIP as our canonical bridge, $APE, $USDC, and other key assets on ApeChain are being upgraded to a Chainlink Cross-Chain Token (CCT).

This upgrade will make it easier for dApps, communities, and their assets to connect.

— ApeCoin (@apecoin) November 4, 2026

It streamlines the cross-chain infrastructure and instead of having separate token transferring platforms throughout Yuga Labs’ ecosystems it supports them together. In the announcement, no deadline or instructions to holders of ApeChain were revealed.

APE and USDC Will Become Cross-Chain Tokens

APE, USDC, and other critical assets on ApeChain will undergo an upgrade to Chainlink Cross-Chain Tokens, or CCTs. Chainlink’s view on the CCT is a token that is programmed with the ability to send transactions over CCIP. The token developer controls the contracts, pools and cross-chain parameters of the developed tokens.

There are multiple transferring models available for CCTs such as: burn-and-mint, lock-and-mint and lock-and-unlock. This is dependent on the specific configuration of each token on supported chains. ApeChain has not mentioned yet, which model will it use for APE, USDC or other assets.

Read More: Arc Surges $1 Billion in USDC Circulating Supply

CCIP Gives ApeChain One Integration Layer

One of the main benefits of the CCT model is integration simplicity. After the token’s registration, the decentralized application or an aggregator of bridges will make contact with the CCIP router, rather than with each other separately for all the tokens.

This can facilitate dApps and communities within the Yuga Labs ecosystem to help the identical assets on several chains. The token pools also enable issuers to control cross-chain configuration, such as cross-chain transfer limits for each configuration route.

Rate limits are recommended for token pools by Chainlink to curb the amount of value that transacts down the lane over time and lower the operational exposure during an incident.

Yuga Labs Unifies Cross-Chain Infrastructure

The migration brings several Yuga Labs’ products into a common interoperability framework. For the APE and Bored Ape Yacht Club use cases, CCIP is the canonical cross-chain infrastructure for ApeChain, Chainlink explained.

The handling of ApeChain has shifted from adding another bridge to changing its current cross-chain standard to one framework that facilitates token transfer as well as application messaging.

Additionally, CCIP enables programmed token transfers where tokens and instructions are transferred among chains, for example when handling deposits, staking, and swaps. ApeChain and Chainlink have not announced the specifics of the ApeChain fee structure, nor have they come up with the final list nor timetable.

Read More: Kraken USDC Jumps 30% While EURC Trading Nears 1B in Circle Stablecoin Expansion
